data.title: What Every Programmer Should Know About Enumerative Combinatorics
data.author: muragekibicho
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于枚举组合学对程序员的重要性及其实际应用的讨论

不同观点：
• **qsort**：认为文章内容有些混乱，尤其是对熟悉材料的人来说。从数学角度质疑主题的选择，建议可以讨论Stirling数等更实用的问题，或从程序员角度讨论如何高效生成子集、排列等。同时指出将阶乘数系和二项式基数作为计算机架构的替代方案是不准确的。
• **giomasce**：认为枚举组合学并非每个程序员都需要了解的内容，反对使用吸引眼球的标题。
• **simpaticoder**：认为文章像是程序员在面试问题后深入研究的产物，但并不一定适合写成广泛关注的文章，类似于对特定编程问题的过度泛化。
• **rck**：认为Rota's twelvefold way涵盖了非专业组合学所需的大部分计数问题，并能解决大部分离散概率问题。
• **qazxcvbnm**：指出计数结构与整数编码密切相关，讨论了如何将结构转换为整数编码及反向操作的方法。
• **getnormality**：认为程序员最需要了解的是组合数据结构，利用现有库如Python的itertools可以更清晰、简洁地实现组合迭代。
• **jmount**：作为组合学爱好者，推荐使用Master定理来处理大多数计数问题，并推荐了深入学习组合学的参考书。
• **barbazoo**：不理解文章为何认为枚举组合学对程序员是相关且重要的主题。

补充讨论：
• **johnisgood**：提问整数分解与整数分区的区别，具体例子中对分区与分解的数量不一致表示困惑。
• **tmoertel**：关注GitHub注入的隐藏或双向Unicode文本问题。
• **Etheryte**：质疑文章标题插图与实际内容的匹配性。
• **louthy**：建议程序员忽略标题中带有“every”的文章。
• **pestatije**：对louthy的观点表示疑问。
• **relaxing**：分享了关于组合学的歌曲，表达了对组合学趣味性的感受。

争议焦点：
• 文章内容是否适合程序员，特别是标题是否夸大其重要性。
• 文章主题选择是否合理，是否应包括更多实用或基础的组合学内容。
• 文章内容与标题插图的匹配性问题。

总结：评论中主要争议在于枚举组合学对程序员的实际重要性及文章内容的适当性，同时也有对组合学具体概念和实现细节的讨论。

data.title: Hackers Weaponize KeePass Password Manager
data.author: mosiuerbarso
data.article_summary: 黑客利用开源密码管理器KeePass传播恶意软件并窃取密码。攻击者通过修改KeePass安装程序并使用可信证书分发名为KeeLoader的恶意加载器。他们利用恶意广告将用户引导至虚假下载页面，安装后的KeePass包含窃取用户凭证的组件。KeeLoader修改KeePass的可执行文件，设置自启动并部署Cobalt Strike信标，信标伪装成JPG文件，仅在访问密码数据库时激活，以躲避检测。被盗数据以CSV格式保存，并通过手动机制提取。攻击基础设施与知名初始访问代理（IAB）相关，涉及多起高调的勒索软件攻击。此次攻击展示了恶意广告和复杂恶意软件投放工具的有效性，强调了加强网络安全 vigilance 和检测能力的必要性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：KeePass 安装程序被恶意修改并重新签名以传播恶意软件的事件及其背后的责任归属

不同观点：
• [fwn] 认为此次攻击并不是 KeePass 本身的问题，而是一个信任问题。他指出，攻击的源头在于搜索引擎上的恶意广告，这些广告将用户引导至虚假下载页面，最终诱使用户安装假应用。因此，他认为这是滥用广告系统的问题，而非 KeePass 的安全漏洞。
• [fwn] 同时提到自己对 KeePass 有一些其他方面的保留意见，但在这起事件中，KeePass 并不是问题所在。

补充讨论：
• [fwn] 强调了威胁行为者如何“武器化”不负责任的广告。他认为，广告平台在审核和验证广告内容方面的不足，是导致此类攻击成功的重要因素。
• 争议的焦点在于责任的归属：一部分人可能认为 KeePass 应该对用户安装过程中的安全性负责，而另一部分人（如 [fwn]）则认为这是广告生态系统中的信任问题，KeePass 只是被利用的工具。

总结来看，评论主要围绕事件的根本原因和责任归属展开讨论，具体涉及 KeePass 本身的安全性及其在事件中的角色，以及广告平台在防止恶意广告传播中的责任。

44019453.article_content:
Home
cyber security
Hackers Weaponize KeePass Password Manager to Spread Malware and Steal Passwords
Hackers Weaponize KeePass Password Manager to Spread Malware and Steal Passwords
cyber security
Cyber Security News
Malware
Published on
May 13, 2025
By
Aman Mishra
Supply Chain Attack Prevention
Follow Us on Google News
Threat actors have successfully exploited the widely-used open-source password manager, KeePass, to spread malware and facilitate large-scale password theft.
The attack, which was reported by WithSecure’s Incident Response team, involved modifying and re-signing KeePass installers with trusted certificates to deliver a custom malware loader dubbed KeeLoader.
Malware Delivery Through KeePass
The infection chain began with malvertising campaigns on popular search engines like Bing and DuckDuckGo, directing users to fraudulent download pages masquerading as official KeePass sites.
- Advertisement -
Once installed, the modified KeePass software included components designed not only to manage passwords but also to exfiltrate
user credentials
.
KeeLoader, as analyzed by WithSecure, modifies KeePass’s executable files, namely
KeePass.exe
and
ShInstUtil.exe
, to incorporate malicious functionality.
Upon installation, this trojanized version of KeePass sets up an autorun registry key, ensuring persistence and stealthily deploying a Cobalt Strike beacon.
This beacon masquerades as a legitimate JPG file, using RC4 encryption for concealment, and is triggered only when a password database is accessed, evading conventional sandbox detection.
Credential Theft and Data Exfiltration
The malware systematically extracts KeePass database information, including account details and passwords, saving these in CSV format locally under a random integer filename.
According to the
Report
, this method implies a manual retrieval mechanism, likely through the activated Cobalt Strike beacon, reducing the digital footprint of the attack.
The campaign’s infrastructure revealed connections to a notorious Initial Access Broker (IAB), linked to several high-profile ransomware attacks over the past two years.
The attackers utilized a sophisticated mix of domain registration on Namecheap, hosting on Cloudflare, and leveraging legitimate certificates to sign their malware, employing a three-month validity span for HTTPS certificates from Google Trust Services.
This attack underscores the effectiveness of malvertising in the cybercriminal toolkit, showcasing a shift towards more technically sophisticated and stealthier malware droppers.
The continuous development of KeePass trojans indicates a trend towards simultaneous network access compromise and digital identity theft, contributing to an ever-growing ransomware ecosystem.
The overlap with tactics of known ransomware groups like
Black Basta
and BlackCat, coupled with the usage of initial access malware, malvertising, and custom loaders, suggests a well-connected and resourced operation.
However, discrepancies, such as the ransom note mimicking Akira ransomware but with unique identifiers, complicate attribution attempts, pointing towards potential “as-a-service” operations or actors operating independently.
This incident reveals the persistent threat from ransomware, exacerbated by a robust underground market for cyber tools and services.
The continuous evolution of attack vectors, especially through trusted software like KeePass, necessitates enhanced vigilance and advanced detection capabilities across the cybersecurity industry.

data.title: Last NeXT Computer Website
data.author: behnamoh
data.article_summary: 本文简要介绍了Alexa Internet自1996年起向互联网档案馆捐赠爬虫数据的情况，这些数据经过一段时间后会添加到Wayback Machine。具体展示了一个2000年苹果公司企业技术支持网站的存档页面，该页面提到NeXTSTEP和OPENSTEP产品线的技术支持信息，并通知某些软件将停止销售。页面还提供了技术支持合同购买信息及免费支持资源链接。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：NextStep软件的历史、技术基础及其与现代操作系统的关系

不同观点：
• 第一种观点：[orionblastar] 指出NextStep软件的技术基础是BSD Unix，并且该操作系统已经开源。他提到Steve Jobs在创建Next公司时选择基于BSD Unix，而不是从头开始，目的是为了提高效率。这一选择后来影响了MacOS X的诞生。该评论者还提供了一个链接，可以找到旧版NextStep软件，并提到通过GNUStep项目可以在Linux上实现类似的图形用户界面。

补充讨论：
• [技术细节] NextStep基于BSD Unix，并且与MacOS有技术上的传承关系，特别是在MacOS X的开发过程中起到了重要作用。
• [开源性质] NextStep和MacOS都具有开源性质，这使得它们在开发者社区中具有一定的影响力和使用价值。
• [模拟和移植] 通过模拟器可以运行旧的NextStep软件，GNUStep项目则提供了一种在Linux上实现类似NextStep图形用户界面的方法，显示出该技术在不同操作系统环境中的可移植性和适应性。

争议焦点：
• 目前在该评论中未见明显争议，但可能存在的争议点包括不同操作系统历史发展中的技术选择是否最优，以及开源技术对现代操作系统发展的实际影响。

44019104.article_summary: 本文简要介绍了Alexa Internet自1996年起向互联网档案馆捐赠爬虫数据的情况，这些数据经过一段时间后会添加到Wayback Machine。具体展示了一个2000年苹果公司企业技术支持网站的存档页面，该页面提到NeXTSTEP和OPENSTEP产品线的技术支持信息，并通知某些软件将停止销售。页面还提供了技术支持合同购买信息及免费支持资源链接。
44019104.comments_summary:

不同观点：

• [开源性质] NextStep和MacOS都具有开源性质，这使得它们在开发者社区中具有一定的影响力和使用价值。

争议焦点：
• 目前在该评论中未见明显争议，但可能存在的争议点包括不同操作系统历史发展中的技术选择是否最优，以及开源技术对现代操作系统发展的实际影响。

data.title: Spaced repetition systems have gotten way better
data.author: domenicd
data.article_summary: 文章主要介绍了间隔重复系统（Spaced Repetition Systems, SRS）在学习和记忆中的应用，特别是其最新改进算法FSRS（Free Spaced Repetition Scheduler）。传统的间隔重复系统如SuperMemo-2通过固定的指数间隔来安排复习，但这种方法较为机械且可能导致挫折感。FSRS通过机器学习算法，根据每个记忆项目的难度、稳定性和检索概率动态调整复习间隔，更有效地对抗“遗忘曲线”。这种新方法提高了学习效率，减少了不必要的重复，使得记忆过程更为高效和个性化。文章还提到，使用FSRS不需要深入了解其技术细节，只需享受其带来的好处即可。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Anki的使用体验及其改进建议，包括数据模型、用户界面、算法优化以及与其他工具的比较

不同观点：
• amluto认为Anki的数据模型不够灵活，缺乏对笔记集合的有效管理和分享机制，且导入导出功能不佳，整体体验较为封闭和笨重。
• 300hoogen分享了通过Anki快速掌握大学课程的实际案例，强调了Anki在应试中的高效性，但也暗示了这种方法可能存在“作弊”的道德问题。
• Knork-and-Fife介绍了一种自制学习工具的旧方法，认为尽管不如Anki便捷，但能带来更好的掌控感，并质疑如果Anki当时已有类似算法，自己是否会转向使用。
• bearjaws对Anki及 spaced repetition的实际效果提出质疑，认为尽管流行多年，但用户在长期坚持上仍有困难，并提出一种强制学习的手机解锁设想。
• iandanforth提到曾因Anki的算法问题写过批评文章，表示可能会重新尝试Anki，以观察其他问题是否有所改善。
• clircle询问如何将spaced repetition应用于商业知识工作，表现出对这种方法在非学术领域的兴趣。
• keiferski认为Anki的算法优化并不关键，UI设计和用户体验的改善才是吸引更多用户的核心。
• JackDanMeier介绍了自己开发的受Anki启发的产品，增加了LLM评分和ELI5解释功能，并提供了免费使用的链接。
• amelius对Anki的复杂性表示困惑，寻求简化的使用方法和语言学习卡片的推荐资源。
• broast提到使用ChatGPT进行Anki风格的测验，展示了一种利用现代AI工具进行学习的新方式。
• entropie因Anki无法与其自定义笔记系统整合，最终自行开发了spaced repetition后端系统，并提供了开源链接。
• Pooge分享了自己通过Anki学习大量日语词汇和汉字的成功经验，强调了坚持练习的重要性。
• linux2647推荐了SaySomethingIn的语言学习课程，强调其基于spaced repetition的听力和口语训练方法。
• c7b询问是否存在适用于长时间间隔复习的算法或插件，表现出对自定义复习节奏的需求。

补充讨论：
• Anki的算法和数据模型是主要争议点，部分用户认为其功能强大但使用不便，尤其是数据管理和分享方面。
• 用户对Anki的UI设计和易用性存在不满，认为其对新手和普通用户不够友好。

• 有用户自行开发了替代工具或方法，以解决Anki的不足，展示了技术娴熟用户的自助解决方案。
• 对spaced repetition的应用场景和算法优化存在多样化需求，包括在非学术领域和长时间间隔复习中的应用。

44020591.article_content:
Spaced repetition recap
Mastering any subject is built on a foundation of knowledge: knowledge of facts, of heuristics, or of problem-solving tactics. If a subject is part of your full-time job, then you’ll likely master it through repeated exposure to this knowledge. But for something you’re working on part-time—like myself
learning Japanese
—it’s very difficult to get that level of practice.
The same goes for subjects in school: a few hours of class or homework a week is rarely enough to build up an enduring knowledge base, especially in fact-heavy subjects like history or medicine. Even parts of your life that you might not think of as learning-related can be seen through this lens: wouldn’t all those podcasts and Hacker News articles feel more worthwhile, if you retained the information you gathered from them indefinitely?
Spaced repetition systems are one of the most-developed answers to this problem. They’re software programs which essentially display flashcards, with the prompt on the front of the card asking you to recall the information on the back of the card. You can read more about them
in Andy’s notes
, or get a flavor from the images below drawn from my personal collection:
What gives these programs their name is how they space out repeatedly prompting you to review the same card, depending on how you self-grade your response. Increasing intervals after correct answers prevents daily reviews from piling up. This is how you can, for example, learn 10 new second-language words a day (3,650 per year!) with only 20 minutes of daily review time.
(If you’re still unconvinced and have some time to spare, I suggest Michael Nielsen’s post
Augmenting Long-term Memory
.)
Improving the scheduling algorithm
So far, this is all well-known. But what’s less widely known is that a quiet revolution has greatly improved spaced repetition systems over the last couple of years, making them significantly more efficient and less frustrating to use. The magic ingredient is a new scheduling algorithm known as
FSRS
, by
Jarrett Ye
.
To understand how these systems have improved, first let’s consider how they used to work. Roughly speaking, you’d get shown a card one day after creating it. If you got it right, you’d get shown it again after 6 days. If you get it right a second time, it’d be next scheduled for 15 days later. If you get the card right three times in a row, then it’s 37.5 days later. In general, after the 6-day interval, there’s an exponential backoff, defaulting to 6 × 2.5
times correct + 1
. You can see how, if you keep getting the card right, this can lead to a large knowledge base, with only a small number of reviews per day!
But what if you get it wrong? Then, you’d reset back to day 1! You’d see the card again the next day, then 6 days after that, and so on. (Although missing the card can also adjust its “ease factor”, i.e. the base in the exponential that is by default set to 2.5.) This can be a fairly frustrating experience, as you experience a card ping-ponging between long and short intervals.
If we step back, we realize that this scheduling system (called “SuperMemo-2”) is pretty arbitrary. Where does the rule of 1, 6, 2.5
times correct + 1
, reset back on failure come from? It turns out it was
developed by a college student in 1987
based on his personal experiments. Can’t we do better?
Recall
the theory behind spaced repetition
: we’re trying to beat the “forgetting curve”, by testing ourselves on the material “just before we were about to forget it”. It seems pretty unlikely that the forgetting curve for every single piece of knowledge is the same: that no matter what I’m learning, I’ll be just about to forget it after 1 day, then 6 more days, then 15, etc. And sure, we can throw in some modifications to the ease factor, but it’s still pretty unlikely that the ideal review schedule is a perfect exponential, even if you let the base vary a bit in response to feedback.
One of many illustrations of the forgetting curve. This one seems to have originated in
a lecture on osmosis.org
.
The insight of the FSRS algorithm is to concretize our goal (testing “just before we are about to forget”) as a prediction problem:
when does the probability of recalling a card drop to 90%?
. And this sort of prediction problem is something that machine learning systems excel at.
Some neat facts about how FSRS works
The above insight—let’s apply machine learning to find the right intervals, instead of using an arbitrary formula—is the core of FSRS. You don’t really need to know how it works to benefit from it. But here’s a brief explanation of some of the details, since I think they’re cool.
FSRS calls itself a “three-component” model because it uses machine learning to fit curves for three main functions:
Difficulty, a per-card number between 1 and 10 roughly representing how difficult the card is
Stability, which is how long a card takes to fall from 100% probability of recall to 90% probability of recall
Retrievab

data.title: Thank you Google for breaking my YouTube addiction
data.author: ambigious7777
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了YouTube近年来在内容推荐上的变化，指出其变得不如以往有趣和引人入胜。过去，YouTube根据用户的订阅和观看历史推荐相关内容，使用户 mildly addictive（轻微上瘾）。然而，随着算法主页的引入，推荐变得更密集和个性化，导致用户沉迷。但最近，YouTube似乎故意让内容变得无聊，重复推荐相同视频，甚至忽视用户的长期兴趣和搜索历史，导致体验下降。文章讽刺地称赞Google可能出于伦理考虑，故意让YouTube变得不那么吸引人，从而减少用户的上瘾程度，认为这是“不做恶”的表现。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：YouTube用户体验的变化与问题

不同观点：
• [openplatypus] 认为YouTube的推荐算法非常不准确，与其隐私设置有关，且平台上的硬件评测内容变得充满赞助和偏见，导致其对YouTube的信任度降低，并提到许多创作者已转移到Nebula平台。
• [danielbln] 指出YouTube的Shorts功能非常容易上瘾，尤其是当观看历史被关闭时，Shorts也无法使用，这可能是用户体验变化的一部分。
• [throwaway519] 表示无法在不登录的情况下观看YouTube内容，认为YouTube作为开放视频平台正在逐渐消亡。
• [yodsanklai] 认为Google通过AI优化用户参与度，但这不一定带来良好的用户体验，并特别提到隐藏 dislike 按钮后，视频质量判断变得困难。
• [unyttigfjelltol] 享受每天空白的YouTube feed，认为这样可以避免算法推送的低质内容，仅观看自己真正喜欢的内容。
• [loloquwowndueo] 提到广告过多使其减少使用YouTube，尤其是在移动设备上，认为不值得为低质内容付费去除广告。
• [perching_aix] 认为通过标记不感兴趣的视频和频道可以改善推荐内容，暗示用户可以主动改善体验。
• [meetingthrower] 抱怨YouTube反复推荐已经多次跳过的视频，认为算法未能有效理解用户偏好。
• [Xss3] 质疑YouTube是否对其搜索算法进行过A/B测试，怀疑新算法是否真的优于旧版本。

补充讨论：
- YouTube推荐算法的准确性和用户隐私设置之间的关系。
- Shorts功能的成瘾性和其对整体用户体验的影响。
- 用户对YouTube广告数量和质量的抱怨。
- 对YouTube隐藏dislike按钮的批评与用户寻找替代方案的努力。
- 用户主动调整推荐内容的可能性与效果。
- 对YouTube搜索算法变化的怀疑与争议。

争议焦点：YouTube算法是否优化了用户体验，尤其是推荐内容的相关性和广告的数量。

44020653.article_content:
Over the past few years, Google has done a surprisingly great job of making YouTube less interesting and engaging — and in turn, less addictive. Maybe they've got some ethical guidelines in the top management now? If so, well done, Google.
Back in the day, when YouTube was mostly about your subscriptions, it was mildly addictive. You’d watch a C++ talk, and the sidebar would actually show you other useful C++ videos. It was relevant, and it kept you watching without feeling like you were drowning in content.
Then they introduced the algorithmic home feed, and that’s when things got intense. You’d open YouTube and get hit with an endless grid of videos tailored to your weird, eclectic mix of interests. Every refresh was like, “Oh, wow, more stuff I didn’t even know I wanted to watch!” It was like YouTube was infinite.
Now? Now it feels like YouTube is trying to bore us into logging off. The homepage just recycles the same 10-20 videos for weeks. It's like a kid in high school trying really hard to expand two sentences into a required 2-page essay by
increasing the line height and font size
, and re-phrasing the same point over and over again.
YouTube app on Apple TV feels particularly empty. The same few videos shuffled on each row.
Watch two bee videos, and suddenly YouTube decides you’re a bee person for life. Over a decade of watch history, interests, searches, playlists — none of that matters anymore. The user is into bees now.
The search now serves up a couple of videos from channels you've interacted with, prioritizing them over the actual relevance, throws in completely unrelated recommendations, and then sprinkles random Shorts on top. It’s like they’re trying to convince you there’s nothing good left to watch.
Interested in nautical route planning algorithms? Sure, but what about sexy girls and cars?
Honestly, it’s kind of brilliant. If you wanted to make YouTube less addictive, this is how you’d do it — by making it feel pointless and lame. So, thanks, Google. You're actually doing the "don't be evil" thing!

data.title: Crypto has become the ultimate swamp asset
data.author: vnorilo
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了加密货币如何从一种梦想超越政治的资产变为充满自利行为的“沼泽”资产。文章将特朗普总统任期内的大量利益冲突与区块链上的巨额加密货币交易相比较，指出后者同样充斥着自利和腐败。文章发表于2025年5月17日的《Leaders》版块，同时还简要提及其他话题，如欧洲的言论自由问题、特朗普的贸易战、墨西哥法治状况以及人工智能管理等。文章强调了加密货币领域存在的严重自利问题，并将其与政治领域的类似问题进行对比。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：加密货币的现状、应用前景、面临的问题以及其在社会中的角色

不同观点：
• keiferski认为，加密货币的初衷是技术人员以开放的精神创造的，但后来被金融行业利用，通过不道德的手段赚钱，同时破坏了其原有的哲学。他还指出，媒体和金融行业的关系以及原始的网络文化的消失，导致了这个简单故事没有广泛传播。他希望比特币能更早发布，以在更合适的文化环境中发展。

• swalsh认为，加密货币应在人工智能时代得到广泛应用，特别是在不同平台的代理之间建立兼容的经济层。他提出了一个具体的方案，使用如USDC等稳定币，并利用现有的区块链网络来实现快速交易，构建一个开放的生态系统，而不是封闭的。

• simonw则担心加密货币的安全问题，特别是高价值资产拥有者面临的绑架风险，以及由于密码丢失而导致资产无法找回的问题。他认为这些问题可能会阻碍加密货币的主流采用。

• zkmon指出，加密货币百万富翁的投资行为可能会推高房地产等真实世界资产的价格，对普通投资者产生影响。

• noisy_boy对加密开发者的日常工作体验与对冲基金中的类似角色有何不同感到好奇，希望得到实际工作在这些领域的人的看法。

• jbverschoor对讨论表现出不耐烦，认为对加密货币的批评可以适用于任何货币，希望转向其他话题。

• ionwake以讽刺的语气评论讨论者订阅《经济学人》杂志的情况，暗示讨论者对经济话题的关注。

• rimbo789认为加密货币从一开始就应该被严格监管，甚至应被禁用，因为其主要用途似乎是非法活动，没有见到有价值的应用案例。

• hengheng认为讨论中缺乏对加密货币未来发展的全面思考，特别是如果不对其进行监管，法律秩序会受到什么影响。他还用特朗普的例子来说明当前体制下存在的潜在问题，并指出需要更深入地探讨加密货币对社会的长远影响。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于加密货币的应用前景和安全性。keiferski和swalsh看好其技术潜力，而simonw和rimbo789则担心其安全性和潜在的非法用途。
• hengheng提出了一个更宏观的问题，即加密货币对法律秩序和社会结构的长远影响，呼吁更全面的讨论。
• 讨论还涉及到加密货币对真实世界经济的影响，如推高房地产价格等。

总的来说，讨论围绕加密货币的技术潜力、安全性、监管需求以及其对社会经济的长远影响展开，展现了不同观点之间的对立与思考。

data.title: Internet Phone Book
data.author: surprisetalk
data.article_summary: 《Internet Phone Book》创刊于2025年，是一本年度出版物，探索丰富的网络诗歌资源，包含文章、随笔以及数百名设计师、开发者、作家、策展人和教育家的个人网站目录。创刊号在线上24小时内售罄，目前可在特定书店、社区空间和图书馆购买。此外，该书还将举办一系列书展活动，如在鹿特丹、雅典和首尔等地。读者可订阅邮件列表以获取再版和活动通知。如有意承办活动或销售此书，可联系出版方。照片由Ana Šantl拍摄。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：20世纪90年代中期互联网信息获取的方式与今天的对比

不同观点：
• **观点一**：在20世纪90年代中期，关于网站的信息非常有限，搜索引擎不够强大，获取网站信息的主要途径是通过印刷书籍。这种书籍类似于电话簿，但规模较小。持此观点的人以自己的亲身经历为例，提到他最早的网站知识来源于这种印刷的书籍，并认为这种信息获取方式与今天的互联网搜索引擎有很大不同。

• **观点二**：有人认为，这种印刷书籍形式的信息获取方式正在现代重新出现。持此观点的人指出，30年后，这种书籍形式正在“重生”，暗示可能存在对早期信息获取方式的某种怀旧或复古趋势，也可能与现代对数字信息疲劳有关。

补充讨论：
• 印刷书籍作为早期互联网资源获取的主要方式，具有历史意义，并且这种形式与现代搜索引擎的强大功能形成鲜明对比。
• 关于“书籍形式重生”的讨论表明，某些过去的信息传播方式在现代可能仍有其价值或吸引力，反映了技术发展中的周期性现象。
• 争议焦点可能在于，现代搜索引擎是否完全替代了所有其他信息获取方式，还是某些传统方式仍然具有不可替代的优势。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：12ft.io及类似工具的实用性和替代方案

不同观点：
• washmyelbows认为12ft.io在获得一定知名度后迅速失去了实用性，暗示该工具可能因为受欢迎而导致效率或功能下降。

• aspenmayer提供了关于绕过付费墙的替代方案，推荐使用"Bypass Paywalls Clean"项目，并解释了其手动更新付费墙列表的方法，认为这种方法更为简单直接。

• sylware提出了对反JavaScript付费墙工具的需求，表明当前可能缺少针对JavaScript付费墙的有效解决方案。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于12ft.io的实用性及其在受欢迎后的表现，用户washmyelbows对其有效性提出质疑。

• aspenmayer的评论引出了一个具体的替代工具"Bypass Paywalls Clean"，并分享了其手动操作的经验，为其他用户提供了不同的选择。

• sylware的评论指出了一个潜在的市场需求，即针对JavaScript付费墙的解决方案，目前讨论中尚未有具体工具被提及。

• 不同用户根据自己的使用经验和需求提出了对工具的看法和建议，展现了在付费墙绕过工具选择上的多样性。

data.title: Postgres with data branching and PII anonymization
data.author: simonklee
data.article_summary:
Xata 推出了全新的 PostgreSQL 平台，强调数据分枝和 PII（个人身份信息）匿名化功能，目标是解决大规模使用 Postgres 时的技术与组织挑战。该平台具有以下特点：

1. **即时写时复制分枝**：快速创建包含生产数据的开发和预览环境。
2. **数据匿名化**：确保开发环境中的数据不包含 PII，符合合规要求。
3. **存算分离**：通过分布式存储系统实现，支持 AWS、GCP、Azure 或自建环境。
4. **零停机**：通过 pgroll 项目实现无停机模式下的模式变更和版本升级。
5. **高性能与成本效益**：适用于大规模数据处理，具有竞争力。

43992908.article_content:
Xata: Postgres with data branching and PII anonymization
Relaunching Xata as "Postgres at scale". A Postgres platform with Copy-on-Write branching, data masking, and separation of storage from compute.
Author
Tudor Golubenco
Date published
May 14, 2025
Here at Xata, we’ve been quietly busy (re)building a new PostgreSQL platform from scratch. We've incorporated everything we learned from operating a Postgres data platform for over four years, combined with feedback from our customers and our analysis of the gaps in the current market.
The result is an entirely
new Postgres service
that:
Has instant Copy-on-Write branches with data.
Includes data anonymization so that developer branches don’t accidentally contain PII.
Is cloud-agnostic, installable in your own AWS/GCP/Azure account, or even on-prem.
Separates storage from compute with a distributed storage system accessed over NVMe/TCP.
Offers a performance/cost ratio that is very competitive at scale.
We'll dive into the technical details shortly, but let's first talk about who this Postgres platform is for.
Postgres at scale
Our goal is to address the challenges teams face when using Postgres at scale. When we say "scale", we don't only mean technical dimensions like data volume, number of CPUs, GB of RAM, or vertical/horizontal scaling capabilities. While these are included in our definition of "at scale", we also mean organizational challenges such as:
Zero-downtime requirements
when applying schema changes or major version upgrades.
Testing database changes or training AI models on
realistic data sets
that resemble the production data, but without any PII or sensitive data in them.
Fast, cost-efficient
ephemeral environments for developers.
Security and compliance
for companies that deal with sensitive data.
Let’s start by looking at
staging and dev
use cases, and then we’ll be talking about
prod
use cases as well.
Staging and dev use cases
Copy-on-Write branches are a great way to quickly spin up preview or development environments with production data, even when dealing with very large datasets. But on their own, they come with two major limitations:
By design, the branches contain exactly the same data as the parent database,
including private PII/PHI or any other sensitive data
. This often violates compliance requirements and risks exposing data to developers.
When it comes to schema changes, branching-out solves only half of the problem.
The other half is merging back in
. Copy-on-Write branches don't provide a mechanism to safely apply the changes you tested in a branch back to your production environment.
Fortunately, we've been working on these exact problems for quite some time now, through two open-source projects:
pgstream
- PostgreSQL replication with DDL changes, now also with masking/anonymization.
pgroll
- Zero-downtime, reversible, schema changes for PostgreSQL.
The new Xata platform combines these projects with Copy-on-Write branches, creating a complete, safe, and consistent developer workflow for PostgreSQL.
The best part is that
you can use Xata even if you are not looking to change your production Postgres service
. Xata works with and improves your existing PostgreSQL service, whether it's AWS RDS, Amazon Aurora, GCP CloudSQL, Azure Database, or even self-hosted Postgres.
At a high level, adopting Xata looks something like this:
Your production database stays exactly as it is, no changes necessary.
We create a “staging replica” on the Xata platform.
xata clone
, powered by
pgstream
, copies and anonymizes the data on the fly.
xata branch create
lets you to create instant dev branches from the staging replica. These branches contain realistic, anonymized versions of your production data.
Optionally, use
xata roll
, powered by
pgroll
, to test schema changes and safely apply them with zero-downtime to production.
If you don't want to send any data out of your production environment, even if anonymized, you don't have to: we have a
BYOC
(Bring Your Own Cloud) deployment model where all staging and dev branches run in your AWS/GCP/Azure/other account or even on-prem. More about that later.
Prod use cases
While you can get the Xata benefits without running your production on our platform, doing so gives you cost savings, better performance, and other wins in terms of flexibility, extensions, and support.
Xata uses an architecture that
separates storage from compute.
This brings benefits like:
Scaling compute and storage separately.
Storage has its own redundancy, increasing durability.
Pay only for what you use in terms of storage, without needing to overprovision.
Storage simply grows automatically and unbounded, without the risk of running out of disk space.
While services like Amazon Aurora and Neon also separate storage from compute, the Xata implementation is different because it is done strictly at the storage layer. This means that we didn’t have to modify Postgres at all. We simply run vanilla Postgres, and therefore have
100% P
43992908.article_summary:
Xata 推出了全新的 PostgreSQL 平台，强调数据分枝和 PII（个人身份信息）匿名化功能，目标是解决大规模使用 Postgres 时的技术与组织挑战。该平台具有以下特点：

1. **即时写时复制分枝**：快速创建包含生产数据的开发和预览环境。
2. **数据匿名化**：确保开发环境中的数据不包含 PII，符合合规要求。
3. **存算分离**：通过分布式存储系统实现，支持 AWS、GCP、Azure 或自建环境。
4. **零停机**：通过 pgroll 项目实现无停机模式下的模式变更和版本升级。
5. **高性能与成本效益**：适用于大规模数据处理，具有竞争力。

Xata 可以与现有的 PostgreSQL 服务（如 AWS RDS、Amazon Aurora）无缝协作，无需更改生产数据库。同时，Xata 还提供了 BYOC（自带云）部署模型，确保数据不出生产环境。如果将生产环境直接运行在 Xata 上，还可以获得更多成本和性能优势。

data.author: prismatic

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：苏富比拍卖行一件预估价超过7000万美元的艺术品未能售出的原因及其反映的艺术市场问题。

不同观点：
• [theamk] 认为，此次拍卖失败可能会让公众对艺术市场的健康状况产生怀疑，尤其是当苏富比和卖家自愿将艺术品暴露在不可预测的市场风险中时。这可能会导致买家在面对天价艺术品时更加谨慎，思考是否值得以如此高价购买，以及未来能否以相同价格转售。

• [abxyz] 对文章中的几个关键点感到困惑。预估价为7000万美元，没有最低价格保证，而最高出价达到了6425万美元，接近预估价的90%，但仍未成交。他还质疑文章中提到的50%溢价问题，因为6425万美元的出价实际上只比上次成交价高出30%左右，而7000万美元的预估价仅高出40%。

• [greatgib] 从社会经济角度批评这种高价购买艺术品的行为，认为这是收藏家的FOMO（错失恐惧症）或基于名气的投资。他指出，这种行为与现实世界的经济脱节，花费巨资购买一件并非独一无二的装饰品是不合理的。

• [wewewedxfgdf] 简单地用标题调侃了此次拍卖失败的事件，没有深入讨论。

• [aurizon] 认为，由于俄罗斯寡头的减少，这种天价艺术品的买家变得稀缺，暗示这些买家是过去推动高价艺术品市场的重要力量。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是为何在6425万美元的高价下艺术品仍未售出，尤其是相比预估价的差距并不大。
• 另一个讨论点是天价艺术品市场的合理性，以及买家在面对高风险投资时的谨慎态度。
• 社会经济角度的批评指出高价艺术品市场的非理性，并将其与普通人的经济状况进行对比。
• 俄罗斯寡头减少对艺术品市场的影响也被提及，暗示国际政治经济变化对市场的影响。

data.title: NASA's Voyager 1 Revives Backup Thrusters Before Command Pause
data.author: taubek
data.article_summary: NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory successfully revived backup thrusters on the Voyager 1 spacecraft, which had been considered inoperable since 2004. The move was necessary as the primary thrusters, essential for keeping the spacecraft's antenna指向地球, are experiencing fuel tube clogs that could cause them to fail. The repairs were conducted before a planned pause in communications starting May 4, 2025, when the antenna used to command Voyager 1 will be offline for upgrades. The revived thrusters serve as a backup to ensure the spacecraft's roll motion can be controlled, maintaining its orientation in interstellar space. The Voyager mission team creatively solved the issue of heater failures that caused the primary thrusters to stop working, ensuring the spacecraft's continued operation amidst upcoming communication challenges.

Solar System

5 min read
NASA’s Voyager 1 Revives Backup Thrusters Before Command Pause
Jet Propulsion Laboratory
https://www.jpl.nasa.gov/
May 14, 2025
NASA’s twin Voyager spacecraft, launched in 1977, are now traveling through interstellar space at around 35,000 mph (56,000 kph). This artist’s concept depicts one of the probes speeding away.
Credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech
The mission team wanted to fix the thrusters, deemed unusable decades ago, before the radio antenna that sends commands to the probe went offline for upgrades.
Engineers at NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Southern California have revived a set of thrusters aboard the Voyager 1 spacecraft that had been considered inoperable since 2004. Fixing the thrusters required creativity and risk, but the team wants to have them available as a backup to a set of active thrusters whose fuel tubes are experiencing a buildup of residue that could cause them to stop working as early as this fall.
In addition, the mission needed to ensure the availability of the long-dormant thrusters before May 4, when the Earth-bound antenna that sends commands to
Voyager 1 and its twin Voyager 2
went offline for months of upgrades.
Thruster Clogging
The Voyagers launched in 1977 and are hurtling through interstellar space at around 35,000 mph (56,000 kph). Both spacecraft rely on a set of primary thrusters to gently pivot them up and down as well as to the right and left in order to keep their antennas pointed at Earth so they can send back data and receive commands. Within the primary set of thrusters are other thrusters that control the spacecraft’s roll motion. Seen from Earth, the roll motion rotates the antenna like a vinyl record to keep each Voyager pointed at a guide star it uses to orient itself. Both spacecraft have a primary and backup set for these roll movements.

(Another set of thrusters, intended to change the spacecrafts’ trajectory
during the flybys of the outer planets
,
were revived
on the spacecraft in 2018 and 2019, but they can’t induce roll motion.)
To
manage the clogging tubes
in the thrusters, engineers switch between the sets of primary, backup, and trajectory thrusters of both Voyagers. But on Voyager 1, the primary roll thrusters stopped working in 2004 after losing power in two small internal heaters. Engineers determined the broken heaters were likely unfixable and opted to rely solely on Voyager 1’s backup roll thrusters to orient the star tracker.
“I think at that time, the team was OK with accepting that the primary roll thrusters didn’t work, because they had a perfectly good backup,” said Kareem Badaruddin, Voyager mission manager at JPL, which manages the mission for NASA. “And, frankly, they probably didn’t think the Voyagers were going to keep going for another 20 years.”
But without the ability to control the spacecraft’s roll motion, a variety of issues would arise that might threaten the mission, so the engineering team decided to reexamine the 2004 thruster failure. They began to suspect that an unexpected change or disturbance in the circuits that control the heaters’ power supply had effectively flipped a switch to the wrong position. If they could turn the switch back to its original position, the heaters might work again, enabling them to reactivate the primary roll thrusters and use them if the backup roll thrusters that have been used since 2004 become completely clogged.
Communications Pause
The solution required some puzzle-solving. The team would have to turn on the dormant roll thrusters, then try fixing and restarting the heaters. If, during that time, the spacecraft’s star tracker drifted too far from the guide star, the long-dormant roll thrusters would automatically fire (thanks to the spacecraft’s programming). And if the heaters were still off when they fired, it could trigger a small explosion, so the team needed to get the star tracker pointed as precisely as possible.
It would be a race, and the team faced additional time pressure: From May 4, 2025, through February 2026, Deep Space Station 43 (
DSS-43
), a 230-foot-wide (70-meter-wide) antenna in Canberra, Australia, that’s part of NASA’s
Deep Space Network
, would be undergoing upgrades. It would be offline for most of that time, with brief periods of operation in August and December.
Although the Deep Space Network has three complexes equally spaced around the globe (in Goldstone, California, and Madrid, in addition to Australia) to ensure constant contact with spacecraft as Earth rotates, DSS-43 is the only dish with enough signal power to send commands to the Voyagers.
“These antenna upgrades are important for future crewed lunar landings, and they also increase communications capacity for our science missions in deep space, some of which are building on the discoveries Voyager made,”

data.title: Telegram's Extraordinary Business Model
data.author: justindownes
data.article_summary: Telegram，由杜罗夫兄弟创立的加密消息平台，以仅30名员工和无人力资源部门的精简结构实现了300亿美元的估值，服务超过10亿用户。这一效率比（每人10亿美元）使其成为当代商业的独特案例。与Facebook和Google等拥有庞大员工队伍的公司不同，Telegram通过技术架构，如云计算和分布式系统，实现了高度自动化和低人力干预。其位于迪拜的总部帮助其保持独立运营风格，不受硅谷常规限制。平台强调隐私和自由，提供加密聊天和自毁消息等功能，反映了创始人的反监控和反审查理念。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Telegram的商业模式、运营效率、隐私保护和内容审核问题

不同观点：
• **赞扬Telegram的高效运营模式**：justindownes认为Telegram以极少数员工实现了高估值，是当代商业的 fascinating 案例。他对比了其他科技巨头，强调Telegram在人员配置上的极简和高效。

• **质疑Telegram的审核和内容管理问题**：Gualdrapo指出Telegram在内容审核上投入不足，导致平台上存在非法活动，如毒品销售和非法内容传播。他认为Telegram过度关注盈利而忽视了平台的健康发展。

• **对Telegram员工数量和运营模式的怀疑**：DonsDiscountGas认为文章过于表面化，指出Telegram选择迪拜可能是为了规避审核问题，且像会计和法律等职能可以外包，因此实际员工数量可能具有误导性。

Typically today’s
tech unicorns
would employ thousands of staff across sprawling corporate campuses in order to power a global comms juggernaut, however one messaging platform stands in stark contrast.
Telegram
, the encrypted messaging service founded by the

, has achieved what many consider impossible: a
$30 billion valuation
with just 30 employees and no human resources department. This remarkable efficiency ratio—$1 billion per employee—has made the Dubai-based company one of the most fascinating case studies in contemporary business.
The Billion-User Club With a Skeleton Crew
Most digital platforms serving over a billion users maintain enormous workforces.
Facebook
employs more than 70,000 people, while
Google
counts over 180,000 staff members on its payroll. Telegram, meanwhile, serves its vast
user base
—which recently crossed the billion-user threshold—with what amounts to a modestly sized team that could fit comfortably in a single conference room.
“What Telegram has accomplished represents a fundamental challenge to conventional wisdom about scaling digital services,” explains Dr. Amelia Richardson, professor of digital economics at Oxford University. “They’ve proven that with the right architecture and organisational philosophy, immense scale doesn’t necessarily require immense headcount.”
The Anti-Corporate Corporate Structure
Perhaps the most controversial aspect of Telegram’s operational model is its complete absence of a
human resources department
. While many tech companies have embraced increasingly complex organisational structures with dedicated teams for employee experience, diversity initiatives, and workplace culture, Telegram has opted for a radically different approach.
Pavel Durov
, Telegram’s enigmatic founder and CEO, has been publicly critical of bureaucratic bloat in tech companies. In a
Medium post
that went viral within Silicon Valley circles last year, Durov wrote: “Every person added to a project increases the complexity of communication exponentially. The most efficient organisations solve this equation by keeping teams small and focused.”
This philosophy extends beyond mere staffing numbers. Telegram operates without many of the trappings of contemporary corporate culture—no mandatory team-building exercises, no elaborate performance review systems, and certainly no “open office” concepts designed to foster collaboration.
Technical Architecture as Competitive Advantage
Industry analysts point to Telegram’s technical architecture as a crucial enabler of its lean operations.
Cloud computing
and
distributed systems
allow the platform to scale horizontally without requiring proportional growth in human oversight.
“What’s remarkable about Telegram’s infrastructure is how much they’ve automated,” says Raj Patel, founder of TechStack Ventures. “Their distributed server network spans multiple jurisdictions and can handle traffic surges with minimal human intervention. Most companies would have teams of
site reliability engineers
constantly monitoring these systems.”
The messaging app’s feature set—including
encrypted chats
, large group capacities up to 200,000 members, and extensive bot functionality—is maintained and expanded by a development team that would be considered severely understaffed by industry standards.
The Dubai Factor
Telegram’s choice of
Dubai
as its operational headquarters represents another element of its unconventional strategy. While most major messaging platforms operate from traditional tech hubs like Silicon Valley, Seattle, or London, Telegram’s location in the United Arab Emirates offers distinct advantages.
Dubai’s
business-friendly regulations
, tax efficiency, and strategic position between European and Asian markets create an environment well-suited to Telegram’s independent ethos. The city-state’s commitment to becoming a global technology hub has included incentives that benefit lean, efficient operators like Telegram.
“Dubai allows Telegram to maintain its unique corporate culture without the pressure to conform to Silicon Valley norms,” notes Sarah Al-Jabri, a technology policy researcher at the Dubai Future Foundation. “The regulatory environment here supports their minimalist approach to corporate structure.”
Founded on Principles of Freedom and Privacy
The Durov brothers—Pavel and Nikolai—founded Telegram in 2013 after leaving
VKontakte
(VK), the Russian social network they had previously created. Their departure from Russia came amid pressure from authorities to share user data and censor content.
This origin story continues to shape Telegram’s corporate values and product decisions. The platform’s emphasis on privacy, with features like end-to-end encrypted “Secret Chats” and self-destructing messages, reflects the founders’ commitment to creating communication channels resistant to surveillance and censorship.

data.article_summary: 前DoorDash送餐司机Sayee Chaitainya Reddy Devagiri及其他三人被指控通过虚假客户账户和送餐订单诈骗公司250万美元。他们利用DoorDash员工的登录信息手动分配订单给虚假司机账户，并将未完成的订单标记为已完成，从而骗取款项。每次操作仅需不到五分钟，重复数百次。Devagiri面临最高20年监禁和25万美元罚款，案件将于九月举行状态听证会。同案其他人员已在去年被起诉。

How a DoorDash driver scammed the company out $2.5 million
The driver, along with three others, were charged in October over a fake deliveries ploy.
The driver, along with three others, were charged in October over a fake deliveries ploy.
by
Wes Davis
May 17, 2025, 6:27 PM UTC
Link
Facebook
Threads
Illustration by Alex Castro / The Verge
Wes Davis
is a weekend editor who covers the latest in tech and entertainment. He has written news, reviews, and more as a tech journalist since 2020.
A former DoorDash delivery driver pleaded guilty this week to a wire fraud conspiracy that scammed the company out of over $2.5 million, the US Attorney’s Office in California’s Northern District
announced on Tuesday
. He and others made it happen over a period of months using fake customer accounts, deliveries that never happened, driver accounts, and access to DoorDash employee credentials.
Here’s how the Attorney’s office describes the scheme. The driver, Sayee Chaitainya Reddy Devagiri, placed expensive orders from a fraudulent customer account in the DoorDash app. Then, using DoorDash employee credentials, he manually assigned the orders to driver accounts he and the others involved had created. Devagiri would then mark the undelivered orders as complete and prompt DoorDash’s system to pay the driver accounts. Then he’d switch those same orders back to “in process” and do it all over again. Doing this “took less than five minutes, and was repeated hundreds of times for many of the orders,” writes the US Attorney’s Office.
Related
A pizzeria owner made money buying his own $24 pizzas from DoorDash for $16
Scammers allegedly earned $195,000 referring fake drivers to delivery apps
Devagiri faces up to 20 years in prison and a $250,000 fine, and is scheduled for a status hearing in September. He and four others were
charged in August
for their roles in the scheme, which prosecutors say was carried out between November 2020 and February 2021. The DoorDash employee whose insider credentials they used, Tyler Thomas Bottenhorn, was charged separately in 2022 and pleaded guilty the following year, the Attorney’s Office
wrote in October
.

data.title: JavaScript's New Superpower: Explicit Resource Management
data.author: olalonde
data.article_summary:
这篇文章介绍了“显式资源管理”提案，旨在通过新增的语言特性帮助开发者更精细地管理资源生命周期，如文件句柄和网络连接等。主要特性包括：

1. **using 和 await using 声明**：在资源退出作用域时自动调用其 `dispose` 方法（同步）或 `asyncDispose` 方法（异步），确保资源被正确释放。
2. **[Symbol.dispose]() 和 [Symbol.asyncDispose]()**：分别用于同步和异步资源清理操作。
3. **DisposableStack 和 AsyncDisposableStack**：用于聚合可释放资源的容器。
4. **SuppressedError**：一种新错误类型，用于处理资源释放时出现的错误，避免掩盖其他错误。

提案通过这些特性，帮助开发者编写更健壮和可维护的代码，解决了如流锁定等问题。在示例中，展示了如何通过 `try...finally` 手动释放资源，以及如何使用 `using` 声明自动管理资源释放。未来，这些符号可能集成到Web API中，进一步简化开发。

44012227.article_content:
The
Explicit Resource Management
proposal introduces a deterministic approach to explicitly manage the lifecycle of resources like file handles, network connections, and more. This proposal brings the following additions to the language: the
using
and
await using
declarations, which automatically calls dispose method when a resource goes out of scope;
[Symbol.dispose]()
and
[Symbol.asyncDispose]()
symbols for cleanup operations; two new global objects
DisposableStack
and
AsyncDisposableStack
as containers to aggregate disposable resources; and
SuppressedError
as a new type of error (contain both the error that was most recently thrown, as well as the error that was suppressed) to address the scenario where an error occurs during the disposal of a resource, and potientially masking an existing error thrown from the body, or from the disposal of another resource. These additions enable developers to write more robust, performant, and maintainable code by providing fine-grained control over resource disposal.
using
and
await using
declarations
#
The core of the Explicit Resource Management proposal lies in the
using
and
await using
declarations. The
using
declaration is designed for synchronous resources, ensuring that the
[Symbol.dispose]()
method of a disposable resource is called when the scope in which it's declared exits. For asynchronous resources, the
await using
declaration works similarly, but ensures that the
[Symbol.asyncDispose]()
method is called and the result of this calling is awaited, allowing for asynchronous cleanup operations. This distinction enables developers to reliably manage both synchronous and asynchronous resources, preventing leaks and improving overall code quality. The
using
and
await using
keywords can be used inside braces
{}
(such as blocks, for loops and function bodies), and cannot be used in top-levels.
For example, when working with
ReadableStreamDefaultReader

reader.releaseLock()

44012227.article_summary:
这篇文章介绍了“显式资源管理”提案，旨在通过新增的语言特性帮助开发者更精细地管理资源生命周期，如文件句柄和网络连接等。主要特性包括：

1. **using 和 await using 声明**：在资源退出作用域时自动调用其 `dispose` 方法（同步）或 `asyncDispose` 方法（异步），确保资源被正确释放。
2. **[Symbol.dispose]() 和 [Symbol.asyncDispose]()**：分别用于同步和异步资源清理操作。
3. **DisposableStack 和 AsyncDisposableStack**：用于聚合可释放资源的容器。
4. **SuppressedError**：一种新错误类型，用于处理资源释放时出现的错误，避免掩盖其他错误。

提案通过这些特性，帮助开发者编写更健壮和可维护的代码，解决了如流锁定等问题。在示例中，展示了如何通过 `try...finally` 手动释放资源，以及如何使用 `using` 声明自动管理资源释放。未来，这些符号可能集成到Web API中，进一步简化开发。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：动画的艺术性与商业性之间的平衡

不同观点：
• **观点一：动画是一种艺术表现形式**  
  支持者认为动画是通过视觉、听觉等多种感官传递情感和思想的艺术形式。它不仅仅是娱乐工具，还可以反映社会现实、表达个人思想和哲学。例子包括宫崎骏的作品如《千与千寻》，其丰富的隐喻和细腻的情感表达被视为艺术性的体现。

• **观点二：动画的商业化倾向不可避免**  
  另一部分人认为，动画产业需要盈利，因此商业化是不可避免的趋势。大型制作公司如迪士尼、皮克斯的作品往往需要通过票房、周边商品等途径盈利，导致创作过程中需要考虑市场需求和观众喜好。这种观点认为，艺术性和商业性并非对立，但商业因素往往会影响创作方向。

• **观点三：独立动画更能保持艺术纯粹性**  
  有评论指出，独立动画创作者或小型工作室，由于不受大公司和市场的限制，能够更加自由地表达个人艺术理念。例如，一些欧洲或日本的独立动画短片，往往更具实验性和创新性，但这些作品的市场受众较小，传播范围有限。

• **观点四：动画兼具艺术与商业价值**  
  部分人持折衷态度，认为优秀的动画作品可以同时具备艺术性和商业价值。例如，一些经典动画电影不仅获得了票房成功，还赢得了评论界的赞誉和奖项。这些作品通常在视觉效果、叙事结构和情感共鸣上都有较高水准。

补充讨论：
• **技术进步对动画的影响**  
  有讨论提到，随着CG技术、虚拟现实等新技术的应用，动画的制作方式和呈现效果发生了巨大变化。有人认为技术进步提升了动画的表现力，但也有人担心过度依赖技术会导致创作上的同质化和缺乏创新。

• **文化差异对动画理解的影响**  
  评论中有人指出，不同文化背景的观众对动画的理解和期待不同。例如，日本动画在国际市场上的受欢迎程度与其在国内的表现可能有很大差异，这反映了文化差异对动画作品接受度的影响。

争议焦点：  
  动画创作中艺术性与商业性之间的权衡是主要的争议焦点。部分人认为商业化会削弱艺术表达，而另一些人则认为商业化是动画产业持续发展的必要条件。

data.title: The Magic Hours: The Films and Hidden Life of Terrence Malick
data.author: mitchbob
data.article_summary: 《The Magic Hours》一书探讨了美国导演Terrence Malick的神秘生活和他的电影作品。Malick以其低调和回避公众视野而闻名，他不接受采访，也不在公众场合露面，这让他的生活和创作充满了神秘感。作者John Bleasdale通过深入研究和采访Malick的合作者，如艺术总监Jack Fisk和编辑Billy Weber，揭示了Malick早年生活对电影的影响。Malick出生于1943年，在伊利诺伊州和德州长大，曾在哈佛和牛津学习，最终转向电影制作。他的首部电影《Badlands》以低成本制作，却展现了高深的艺术追求，奠定了其独特的电影风格。Malick的电影让人思考电影的本质和美的真实性，他的作品常常引发两极评价。Bleasdale的书尽管详尽，但因未能直接采访Malick而留下未解之谜。

不同观点：

• **关于电影艺术性的讨论**：
  - [rdtsc] 认为马利克是“最不知名的著名导演”，他的电影更具艺术性，需要观众有特定的心情去欣赏，类似于塔可夫斯基的电影。
  - [popalchemist] 指出马利克的才华在于其诗意的表达，而非讲故事的能力。如果观众能接受电影作为一种精神上的“音诗”，就会喜欢他的作品，否则可能会讨厌。

• **电影制作过程的讨论**：
  - [_m_p] 强调了马利克在电影制作中的实验性编辑过程，指出有些演员的角色在后期被剪掉，例如艾德里安·布罗迪在《红色警戒》中的经历。

• **对评论文章的批评**：
  - [donniefitz2] 批评了一篇关于《红色警戒》的文章，认为其分析不够深入，未能充分体现电影的深层次内容。

• **负面评价**：
  - [ArthurStacks] 简单直接地表示马利克的电影无聊透顶，代表了一部分对马利克作品持负面态度的观众。

• 观众对马利克电影的接受度存在明显分歧。一些人深感共鸣，认为其作品具有深刻的艺术和精神价值；而另一些人则觉得其电影枯燥无趣，难以欣赏。这种分歧尤其体现在对电影叙事方式和艺术表达的不同期待上。

The Magic Hours:
The Films and Hidden Life of Terrence Malick
by
John Bleasdale
.
Kentucky, 257 pp., £31.50, December 2024,
978 1 9859 0119 3
Show More
Show More
T
errence Malick
​ is the quietest of American movie directors. He gives no interviews; he avoids talkshows and festival appearances; he doesn’t feed us stories of what he was doing and why. For decades, he has done his best to avoid being photographed. He isn’t a ‘known American’ or a spokesman for himself in the way of Scorsese, Coppola, Tarantino, Spike Lee or just about any other director. For fifty years he has been involving us in questions about cinema – what it is, what it might be, whether it matters. He has perplexed his admirers; several of his films are regarded by some as masterpieces and by others as misguided asides. Above all, he has insisted on beauty, and his films have us wondering whether beauty is truth or a trick. He is a real person. I met him once and talked with him. He was amiable and decent, or distant.
John Bleasdale’s
The Magic Hours
is both a monument to unstoppable research and, in the end, an admission that even such a thorough inquiry can remain inconclusive. Bleasdale hasn’t been able to talk to Malick, or to his family. But he has interviewed some of his essential companions – notably the art director Jack Fisk and the editor Billy Weber. Bleasdale is especially good on Malick’s early life and the details of it that have appeared in his movies. But he is an observant enough member of Malick’s church to know that wonder can be compromised or limited by the facts.
Terrence Malick was born in 1943 in rural Illinois, but the family home was in Waco, Texas. It was nurturing but troubled: Malick often fought with his father (a geologist of Assyrian descent) and was mindful of many ideas beyond Texas. Aged twelve, he was sent to a private boarding school in Austin, where he excelled in all his classes and became a talented football player. Against his father’s advice, he went to Harvard and fell under the sway of Stanley Cavell (who wrote a fine book,
Pursuits of Happiness
, about comedies of remarriage – films like
The Awful Truth
,
His Girl Friday
and
The Philadelphia Story)
. He spent some of his senior year at the Sorbonne, met Hannah Arendt and travelled to the Black Forest with her letter of introduction to meet Martin Heidegger (Malick’s translation of
The Essence of Reasons
was published a few years later). After graduating in 1965 he went to Oxford as a Rhodes scholar, but didn’t like the cold and damp, and ‘talking to the Brits was like talking underwater.’
He was 23 years old and ‘the world was calling,’ as Bleasdale puts it. He tried journalism, but foundered trying to write about Che Guevara for the
New Yorker
. Briefly, he dated Carly Simon; she listened attentively, she said, ‘as he talked with the kind of fervid enthusiasm for Che that I secretly hoped he might have an iota of for me’. He was very serious, but could be very funny too. He taught at MIT for a year but decided he was a poor teacher, inclined to drift. So he applied to a programme at the school newly opened in Los Angeles by the American Film Institute to improve the minds of Hollywood hotshots. He was in a class with David Lynch and Paul Schrader.
Something in him was set on making movies, though years later he would also adapt the Kenji Mizoguchi film
Sansho the Bailiff
(1954) for the stage. In addition, and almost to demonstrate his caring and not caring, he wrote an early draft of what would become
Dirty Harry
and got the writing credit on
Pocket Money
(1972), in which Lee Marvin and Paul Newman are involved with a small herd of cattle. One critic said it felt like a home movie in which the two actors were killing time. One way or another, Malick was finding a way to get round Hollywood’s rules.
He had hoped to make a film of Walker Percy’s novel
The Moviegoer
, as if inspired by the transcendent moment when the main character, Binx, observes someone who might be William Holden on the streets of New Orleans. Is he the real thing, or a ghost, a technological anticipation of holography, or just the manifestation of an awareness that such gods as Holden had become axiomatic, as much a model for American manhood as Johnny Carson or Bugs Bunny? Instead, in 1973, Malick made an unexpected debut that was arty and high-minded, even though it was called
Badlands
, which made it sound like an exploitation movie. It was made cheaply, in the tradition of B-movie film noirs, with money from the producer Ed Pressman, the computer millionaire Max Palevsky and Malick himself. It was based on the story of a Nebraska hoodlum called Charles Starkweather (Martin Sheen), who in 1957 killed the father of 14-year-old Caril Ann Fugate (Sissy Spacek, 23 at the time), and then took off with her on the lam across the desolate spaces of legend.
Bad
44008412.article_summary: 《The Magic Hours》一书探讨了美国导演Terrence Malick的神秘生活和他的电影作品。Malick以其低调和回避公众视野而闻名，他不接受采访，也不在公众场合露面，这让他的生活和创作充满了神秘感。作者John Bleasdale通过深入研究和采访Malick的合作者，如艺术总监Jack Fisk和编辑Billy Weber，揭示了Malick早年生活对电影的影响。Malick出生于1943年，在伊利诺伊州和德州长大，曾在哈佛和牛津学习，最终转向电影制作。他的首部电影《Badlands》以低成本制作，却展现了高深的艺术追求，奠定了其独特的电影风格。Malick的电影让人思考电影的本质和美的真实性，他的作品常常引发两极评价。Bleasdale的书尽管详尽，但因未能直接采访Malick而留下未解之谜。

data.title: Working with Git Patches in Apple Mail (2023)
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了如何在MacOS的Apple Mail中处理Git补丁。首先，用户需要在邮箱中创建一个“Patches”文件夹，用于存放包含Git补丁的邮件。将补丁邮件移至该文件夹后，导出文件夹并保存到本地。然后在终端中导航到目标项目目录，使用`git apply`命令应用保存的补丁文件。虽然过程相对简单，但建议定期清理本地的“Patches”文件夹以保持整洁。虽然有更自动化的方法，但此流程能满足大多数使用场景。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：通过不同工具和方法处理Git中的补丁文件和邮件发送问题

不同观点：
• **johnrob的观点**：他更喜欢使用普通的文件来替代`git stash`，因为这样更容易列出和浏览之前的编辑内容，并且可以通过grep搜索文件内容。他还提到会复制并编辑diff文件后再应用。

• **palata的观点**：他喜欢使用aerc来处理与Git相关的电子邮件，并且可以与其他电子邮件客户端并行使用，专门为Git相关的邮件打开aerc。

• **teeray的观点**：他提到一个偏离主题的问题，询问是否有一种好的方法使用`git send-email`与需要OAuth的电子邮件主机（如Outlook和Gmail）一起工作。

• **smcameron的观点**：他推荐使用stgit，认为如果经常处理Git和补丁文件，这是一个值得一看的工具。

• **kazinator的观点**：他建议直接在浏览器中查看电子邮件的原始内容，选择全部，复制并粘贴到`git apply`中。这样不需要基于文件的收件箱，并且在某些情况下仍然可能需要复制和粘贴以获取正确的路径。

• **sircastor的观点**：他提出Apple Mail有插件支持，并建议可以编写一个插件来提供应用diff文件的按钮。

补充讨论：
• **工具推荐**：smcameron推荐了stgit作为处理Git补丁的工具，而palata则推荐使用aerc来处理Git相关的电子邮件。

• **技术实现问题**：teeray提出了使用`git send-email`与需要OAuth的电子邮件主机（如Outlook和Gmail）的技术难题，这是一个待解决的问题。

• **实用技巧**：johnrob和kazinator提供了实用的技巧，分别介绍了如何通过普通文件和直接复制粘贴来处理Git补丁文件，强调了便捷性和灵活性。

争议焦点：
• 主要的争议焦点在于如何高效地处理Git补丁文件和邮件发送问题。不同的用户根据自己的经验和需求提出了不同的解决方案，例如使用文件替代`git stash`、使用aerc或stgit工具、直接复制粘贴到`git apply`等，体现了不同的偏好和技术背景。

44020914.article_content:
Working with git Patches in Apple Mail
2023-05-11
Before we begin
You could likely automate this process in a more streamlined way, but for most use cases this workflow should be fine.
I recently covered how to
work with git email patches in Evolution on Linux
, so I thought it would make sense to walk through a similar workflow for those using Apple Mail on MacOS. The idea is essentially the same, with just a little extra work involved.
Create a “Patches” Mailbox
The first thing you’ll need to do is make a new
Patches
mailbox folder inside your existing mail account. Once done, your default Mail sidebar should look similar to the following:
The Apple Mail sidebar with the “Patches” folder present
Applying Patches
Now navigate to the email message containing a
git
patch. Right-click and select
Move to
>
Patches
. Now in the sidebar, right-click your
Patches
folder and select
Export Mailbox…
. You’ll be prompted to save this folder locally. I suggest having a top-level folder named
Patches
to make things consistent.
Inside this folder you should see something similar to the following structure:
The contents of the saved Patches mailbox folder
Once saved, open your terminal, navigate to the project you wish to apply this new patch to:
cd
my-path/very-cool-project
and then run:
git apply ~/Patches/<saved-patches-mailbox-folder>/mbox
Congrats! You’ve successfully applied a git email patch through Apple Mail! Well, kind of. The terminal did most of the
real
work. Just be sure to periodically
purge
your local
Patches
folder to keep things clean!

data.author: sklargh

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对Hell Gate岩石清除项目的不同角度的讨论，包括历史上的风险评估、技术创新以及现代视角的比较。

不同观点：
• [MontagFTB] 提供了关于Hell Gate岩石清除的详细信息链接，引导读者查看维基百科页面以获取更多背景知识。该评论主要是信息分享，没有明确表达立场。

• [dmoy] 提到了另一个名为Darvaza gas crater的“地狱之门”，并将其与Hell Gate项目进行比较，暗示两者都采用了类似的激进方法（炸毁或点燃）。虽然该评论带有调侃性质，但提出了对不同情境下相似方法的思考。

• [monster_truck] 对历史上航运事故的频率（每年1000艘船中有1/50会搁浅）以及技术发现（如同时引爆无限数量的地雷）表示惊讶。质疑这是否真的是第一次有人“大胆尝试”使用 detonators，并提出了对技术上限的疑问。

• [ddulaney] 对过去人们对风险的不同看法表示感慨，指出当时“地表无损坏”被视为新发现的事实。该评论暗示现代社会对风险的接受度可能有所不同，无论这种变化是好是坏。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：虽然没有直接的对立观点，但[monster_truck]对 detonators 的首次使用提出质疑，暗示可能存在历史记录不准确或技术发展脉络不清的问题。

• 技术历史与现代视角的比较：[ddulaney]的评论特别提到了过去与现代在风险评估和管理上的不同，提出了对历史事件在当代可能产生的不同反应的思考。

• 对激进方法的思考：[dmoy]和[ddulaney]的评论都涉及对历史上采用激进手段（如炸毁、点燃）的看法，尽管情境不同，但都引发了对这些方法在现代是否适用的思考。

总结来看，讨论围绕历史上的技术创新、风险管理以及这些事件在现代视角下的不同解读展开。不同的评论者从信息分享、技术质疑、历史反思等多个角度进行了讨论。

data.title: Show HN: Hardtime.nvim – break bad habits and master Vim motions
data.author: m4xshen
data.article_summary:
**hardtime.nvim** 是一个 Neovim 插件，旨在帮助用户改掉不良的 Vim 操作习惯，提高编辑效率。它通过限制短时间内重复按键、提供操作提示以及生成常见不良习惯报告来帮助用户更好地掌握 Vim 运动键。插件推荐使用更高效的运动方式，如相对跳转、单词运动、操作符组合等。

### 主要功能：
- 限制短时间内重复按键。
- 提供 Vim 运动提示。
- 生成常见不良习惯报告。

### 安装与配置：
- 支持通过常见包管理器安装。
- 提供多种配置选项，如禁用特定键、文件类型、提示行为等。

### 使用方法：
- 默认启用，可通过命令启用、禁用或切换。
- 查看提示报告和日志文件。

插件还支持高级自定义配置，如提示显示方式、超时设置等，帮助用户更灵活地优化编辑体验。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Vim编辑器的操作习惯和优化方法

不同观点：
• **AdieuToLogic** 认为Vim的按键布局设计合理，尤其是hjkl导航键位于主行位置，便于右手操作，其他命令也根据使用频率分布在键盘的不同位置，学习Vim可以按照这种按键布局逐步掌握。
• **BrouteMinou** 不赞成逐字符计数的操作方式，更倾向于通过重复按键（如spam "llll"）来快速移动光标，而不是计算具体数字（如"31-l"）。
• **qazxcvbnm** 提出通过增加终端延迟来强制培养更好的操作习惯，这种方法不依赖插件支持，而是通过强制延迟来训练用户本能反应。
• **blahgeek** 基于多年使用Vim的经验，认为重复按h或j键进行上下移动是直观且有效的，尤其在调整按键重复延迟后，比使用数字加命令的方式更符合直觉。
• **marcyb5st** 感谢原帖中提到的方法，但对某些观点持保留意见，如在编辑模式下允许使用Home/End键，认为这些按键在其他文本输入场景中也普遍使用。

补充讨论：
• **mnurzia** 和 **WhyNotHugo** 都提到使用插件或禁用箭头键的方式强迫自己使用hjkl，最终帮助他们提高了Vim操作效率。
• **perrygeo** 坦承自己使用Vim超过20年，但仍在某些导航操作上有坏习惯，认为某些插件功能既帮助揭示了坏习惯，但也可能导致其卸载插件。
• **unshavedyak** 和 **avinassh** 关注插件的兼容性及通用性问题，前者希望将类似功能推广到其他编辑器如Helix，后者则遇到插件冲突问题。
• **n8cpdx** 和 **lylejantzi3rd** 都表达了对VS Code中Vim模拟器和LazyVim安装的类似需求，希望优化现有的Vim使用体验。
• **nickandbro** 提到正在开发类似的工具，并计划增加关卡编辑器功能。
• **SuperManifolds** 分享了使用该插件后成功改掉坏习惯的个人经验，特别提到插件允许自定义规则的功能非常有用。

争议焦点：
• Vim中是否应该避免重复使用h-l或w-W键进行水平移动，一方认为应精确使用数字加命令，另一方则更倾向于通过重复按键快速导航。
• 对Home/End键在编辑模式下的使用存在不同看法，一部分用户认为这些键应被允许，因为它们在其他文本输入场景中也普遍使用。

44020734.article_summary:
**hardtime.nvim** 是一个 Neovim 插件，旨在帮助用户改掉不良的 Vim 操作习惯，提高编辑效率。它通过限制短时间内重复按键、提供操作提示以及生成常见不良习惯报告来帮助用户更好地掌握 Vim 运动键。插件推荐使用更高效的运动方式，如相对跳转、单词运动、操作符组合等。

### 主要功能：
- 限制短时间内重复按键。
- 提供 Vim 运动提示。
- 生成常见不良习惯报告。

### 安装与配置：
- 支持通过常见包管理器安装。
- 提供多种配置选项，如禁用特定键、文件类型、提示行为等。

### 使用方法：
- 默认启用，可通过命令启用、禁用或切换。
- 查看提示报告和日志文件。

插件还支持高级自定义配置，如提示显示方式、超时设置等，帮助用户更灵活地优化编辑体验。
44020734.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Vim编辑器的操作习惯和优化方法

不同观点：
• **AdieuToLogic** 认为Vim的按键布局设计合理，尤其是hjkl导航键位于主行位置，便于右手操作，其他命令也根据使用频率分布在键盘的不同位置，学习Vim可以按照这种按键布局逐步掌握。
• **BrouteMinou** 不赞成逐字符计数的操作方式，更倾向于通过重复按键（如spam "llll"）来快速移动光标，而不是计算具体数字（如"31-l"）。
• **qazxcvbnm** 提出通过增加终端延迟来强制培养更好的操作习惯，这种方法不依赖插件支持，而是通过强制延迟来训练用户本能反应。
• **blahgeek** 基于多年使用Vim的经验，认为重复按h或j键进行上下移动是直观且有效的，尤其在调整按键重复延迟后，比使用数字加命令的方式更符合直觉。
• **marcyb5st** 感谢原帖中提到的方法，但对某些观点持保留意见，如在编辑模式下允许使用Home/End键，认为这些按键在其他文本输入场景中也普遍使用。

补充讨论：
• **mnurzia** 和 **WhyNotHugo** 都提到使用插件或禁用箭头键的方式强迫自己使用hjkl，最终帮助他们提高了Vim操作效率。
• **perrygeo** 坦承自己使用Vim超过20年，但仍在某些导航操作上有坏习惯，认为某些插件功能既帮助揭示了坏习惯，但也可能导致其卸载插件。
• **unshavedyak** 和 **avinassh** 关注插件的兼容性及通用性问题，前者希望将类似功能推广到其他编辑器如Helix，后者则遇到插件冲突问题。
• **n8cpdx** 和 **lylejantzi3rd** 都表达了对VS Code中Vim模拟器和LazyVim安装的类似需求，希望优化现有的Vim使用体验。
• **nickandbro** 提到正在开发类似的工具，并计划增加关卡编辑器功能。
• **SuperManifolds** 分享了使用该插件后成功改掉坏习惯的个人经验，特别提到插件允许自定义规则的功能非常有用。

争议焦点：
• Vim中是否应该避免重复使用h-l或w-W键进行水平移动，一方认为应精确使用数字加命令，另一方则更倾向于通过重复按键快速导航。
• 对Home/End键在编辑模式下的使用存在不同看法，一部分用户认为这些键应被允许，因为它们在其他文本输入场景中也普遍使用。

data.article_summary: BrowserBee 是一个开源的 Chrome 扩展程序，通过自然语言控制浏览器操作。它利用大型语言模型（LLM）解析指令并制定计划，同时使用 Playwright 实现强大的浏览器自动化功能。BrowserBee 注重隐私保护，所有操作均在浏览器内完成（LLM 除外），可安全地与登录网站交互，无需后端基础设施。它支持多种 LLM 提供商，如 Anthropic、OpenAI、Gemini 和 Ollama，并能跟踪 token 使用情况和费用。此外，它还提供多种浏览器工具，如导航、标签页管理、交互、观察、鼠标和键盘操作等，并具有记忆功能，可保存有用的操作序列以便将来使用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕浏览器扩展和LLM（大型语言模型）应用的技术方案、隐私安全、跨浏览器支持及用户体验的讨论。

不同观点：
• **关于信息优化与安全性的讨论：**
  - dataviz1000认为可以通过使用堆叠上下文（stacking context）和缓存DOM结构，将发送给LLM的信息量减少100倍。同时指出Playwright和Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP) 结合会带来安全问题，特别是涉及银行和敏感账户的操作。
  - 他建议自己实现功能，而不是依赖Playwright，并提出通过提示用户点击按钮来处理需要可信事件的场景。

• **关于会话模板化和隐私保护的建议：**
  - nico对项目表示赞赏，并建议增加会话模板化功能，使会话可以像电子邮件模板一样使用占位符标签。同时也提到通过使用本地LLM（如ollama）实现更注重隐私的方案。

• **关于跨浏览器支持的需求：**
  - dbdoskey和donclark提到希望该扩展可以支持Firefox等其他浏览器，指出Mozilla的Orbit未能满足需求。

• **关于类似项目和功能简化的分享：**
  - stoicfungi分享了自己构建类似Chrome扩展的经历，并提到为了简化功能而移除了交互模式。

• **关于内容发送和隐私安全的疑问：**
  - barbazoo和hoppp对内容是否发送到LLM以及是否涉及密码发送提出疑问，质疑项目的隐私安全性。
  - krembo和rizs12提到Chrome Canary已经内置Gemini Nano，无需调用第三方LLM API，并质疑扩展是否符合隐私优先的原则。

• **关于模型选择的讨论：**
  - matula对Ollama模型硬编码为Qwen3和Llama 3.1表示不满，建议增加自定义配置功能以支持用户选择的模型。

• **关于开发历程和未来计划的询问：**
  - m0rde对项目的开发历程和是否依赖AI代理编写代码表示兴趣，并询问了 monetization（商业化）和捐赠的打算。

• **用户遇到的错误问题：**
  - saadshamim报告使用Gemini和OpenAI API时遇到错误，即使使用有效的新API密钥也无法解决。

• **关于LLM执行DOM操作的能力：**
  - 0xd1r询问该扩展是否可以进行DOM操作，例如填写表单，或者是否需要为每个特定网站结构化LLM的响应。

补充讨论：
- 多个评论提到了隐私和安全问题，特别是涉及到与敏感网站（如银行）的交互以及是否将数据发送到LLM。
- 对跨浏览器支持有明确需求，尤其是Firefox用户。
- 用户对模型选择和自定义配置功能有较高期望，希望可以根据个人偏好选择LLM模型。
- 一些用户对项目的技术实现细节（如DOM操作和错误处理）表示关注，并提供了反馈。

BrowserBee 🐝
Your in-browser AI assistant. Control the web with natural language.
BrowserBee.mp4
BrowserBee is a privacy-first open source Chrome extension that lets you control your browser using natural language. It combines the power of an LLM for instruction parsing & planning, and Playwright for robust browser automation to accomplish tasks.
Since BrowserBee runs entirely within your browser (with the exception of the LLM), it can safely interact with logged-in websites, like your social media accounts or email, without compromising security or requiring backend infrastructure. This makes it more convenient for personal use than other "browser use" type products out there.
🎲 Features
Supports major LLM providers such as
Anthropic
,
OpenAI
,
Gemini
, and
Ollama
with more coming soon
Tracks
token use
and
price
so you know how much you're spending on each task
Has access to a wide range of
🕹️ browser tools
(listed below) for interacting and understanding browser state
Uses
Playwright
in the background which is a robust browser automation tool
The
memory
feature captures useful tool use sequences and stores them locally to make future use more efficient
The agent knows when to ask for user's
approval
, e.g. for purchases or posting updates on social media
🕹️ Supported tools
Navigation Tools
browser_navigate
Navigate the browser to a specific URL. Input must be a full URL, e.g.
https://example.com
browser_wait_for_navigation
Wait until network is idle (Playwright).
browser_navigate_back
Go back to the previous page (history.back()). No input.
browser_navigate_forward
Go forward to the next page (history.forward()). No input.
Tab Context Tools
browser_get_active_tab
Returns information about the currently active tab, including its index, URL, and title.
browser_navigate_tab
Navigate a specific tab to a URL. Input format: 'tabIndex|url' (e.g., '1|
https://example.com
')
browser_screenshot_tab
Take a screenshot of a specific tab by index. Input format: 'tabIndex[,flags]' (e.g., '1,full')
Interaction Tools
browser_click
Click an element. Input may be a CSS selector or literal text to match on the page.
browser_type
Type text. Format: selector|text (e.g. input[name="q"]|hello)
browser_handle_dialog
Accept or dismiss the most recent alert/confirm/prompt dialog. Input
accept
or
dismiss
. For prompt dialogs you may append
|text
to supply response text.
Observation Tools
browser_get_title
Return the current page title.
browser_snapshot_dom
Capture DOM snapshot of the current page with options for selector, clean, structure, and limit.
browser_query
Return up to 10 outerHTML snippets for a CSS selector you provide.
browser_accessible_tree
Return the AX accessibility tree JSON (default: interesting‑only). Input 'all' to dump full tree.
browser_read_text
Return all visible text on the page, concatenated in DOM order.
browser_screenshot
Take a screenshot of the current page with options for full page capture.
Mouse Tools
browser_move_mouse
Move the mouse cursor to absolute screen coordinates. Input format:
x|y
(example:
250|380
)
browser_click_xy
Left‑click at absolute coordinates. Input format:
x|y
(example:
250|380
)
browser_drag
Drag‑and‑drop with the left button. Input format:
startX|startY|endX|endY
(example:
100|200|300|400
)
Keyboard Tools
browser_press_key
Press a single key. Input is the key name (e.g.
Enter
,
ArrowLeft
,
a
).
browser_keyboard_type
Type arbitrary text at the current focus location. Input is the literal text to type. Use
\n
for new lines.
Tab Tools
browser_tab_list
Return a list of open tabs with their indexes and URLs.
browser_tab_new
Open a new tab. Optional input = URL to navigate to (otherwise blank tab).
browser_tab_select
Switch focus to a tab by index. Input = integer index from browser_tab_list.
browser_tab_close
Close a tab. Input = index to close (defaults to current tab if blank).
Memory Tools
save_memory
Save a memory of how to accomplish a specific task on a website. Use this when you want to remember a useful sequence of actions for future reference

data.author: coloneltcb
data.article_summary: John L. Young，享年89岁，是网络图书馆**Cryptome**的创始人之一，该平台致力于揭露官方秘密，提供关于言论自由、隐私、加密技术、国家安全等领域的资料。Cryptome成立于1996年，迅速成为发布政府、法院和企业文件的重要平台，特别是在1990年代的“加密战争”期间，成为关键的信息来源。Young还曾支持早期的维基解密，但因反对其商业化而与其决裂。尽管面临FBI、大科技公司的打压，他始终坚持透明性，为公众的知情权而奋斗。作为数字时代的先驱，John的贡献在于推动信息民主化，为公众获取被官方隐藏的信息提供了平台。

43999897.article_content:
John L. Young, who died March 28 at age 89 in New York City, was among the first people to see the need for an online library of official secrets, a place where the public could find out things that governments and corporations didn’t want them to know. He made real the idea – revolutionary in its time – that the internet could make more information available to more people than ever before.
John and architect Deborah Natsios, his wife, in 1996 founded
Cryptome
, an online library which collects and publishes data about freedom of expression, privacy, cryptography, dual-use technologies, national security, intelligence, and government secrecy. Its slogan: “The greatest threat to democracy is official secrecy which favors a few over the many.” And its invitation: “We welcome documents for publication that are prohibited by governments worldwide.”
Cryptome soon became known for publishing an encyclopedic array of government, court, and corporate documents. Cryptome assembled an indispensable, almost daily chronicle of the ‘crypto wars’ of the 1990s – when the first generation of internet lawyers and activists recognized the need to free up encryption from government control and undertook litigation, public activism and legislative steps to do so.  Cryptome became required reading for anyone looking for information about that early fight, as well as many others.
John and Cryptome were also among the early organizers and sponsors of WikiLeaks, though like many others, he later broke with that organization over what he saw as its monetization. Cryptome later published Wikileaks’ alleged internal emails. Transparency was the core of everything John stood for.
John was one of the early, under-recognized heroes of the digital age.
John was a West Texan by birth and an architect by training and trade. Even before he launched the website, his lifelong pursuit of not-for-profit, public-good ideals led him to seek access to documents about shadowy public development entities that seemed to ignore public safety, health, and welfare. As the digital age dawned, this expertise in and passion for exposing secrets evolved into Cryptome with John its chief information architect, designing and building a real-time archive of seminal debates shaping cyberspace’s evolving information infrastructures.
The FBI and Secret Service tried to chill his activities. Big Tech companies like Microsoft
tried to bully him into pulling documents off the internet
. But through it all, John remained a steadfast if iconoclastic librarian without fear or favor.
John served in the United States Army Corps of Engineers in Germany (1953–1956) and earned degrees in philosophy and architecture from Rice University (1957–1963) and his graduate degree in architecture from Columbia University in 1969. A self-identified radical, he became an activist and helped create the community service group Urban Deadline, where his fellow student-activists initially suspected him of being a police spy. Urban Deadline went on to receive citations from the Citizens Union of the City of New York and the New York City Council.
John was one of the early, under-recognized heroes of the digital age. He not only saw the promise of digital technology to help democratize access to information, he brought that idea into being and nurtured it for many years.  We will miss him and his unswerving commitment to the public’s right to know.

data.title: Magic Leap One Bootloader Exploit
data.author: mmastrac
data.article_summary: 该文章介绍了针对Magic Leap One（可能还有其他TX2设备）的漏洞利用代码库（ml1hax）。仓库包含两个主要漏洞的实现：通过Fastboot USB在CBoot上执行代码（利用NVidia的SparseFS解析器）和通过超大的内核设备树blob（kernel-dtb）覆盖CBoot以获得持久代码执行。使用这些漏洞需要自行承担风险，包括将设备变砖的可能性。具体步骤包括准备签名上下文文件、编译并运行利用代码。详细的说明文档尚未完成，适合有技术能力的用户尝试。代码主要使用Rust编写。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Nvidia硬件的bootloader漏洞以及其在如Nintendo Switch等平台上的利用

不同观点：
• [bigyabai] 认为Nvidia商用硬件的bootloader漏洞是一个吸引人的特点，特别是对像Nintendo Switch这样锁定的平台。他指出，这类平台可以从homebrew商店中受益，因为这些商店依赖于bootloader漏洞来进行自制软件的安装和运行。

• [Namidairo] 则对现代Tegra设备在整个生产线中使用相同的SBK（Secure Boot Key）表示惊讶。他认为，基于序列号或芯片ID进行混合应该是更合理的做法，并对当前做法的安全性提出质疑。不过，他也表示乐见Tegra设备的boot chain再次被攻破，暗示出对技术破解的兴趣。

补充讨论：
• [bigyabai] 强调了漏洞对于自制软件社区的价值，特别是对锁定平台的扩展功能和软件自由度的提升。

• [Namidairo] 关注的是设备安全性及厂商在密钥管理上的策略，质疑为何没有采用更复杂的密钥分发方式来增强安全性。

争议焦点：
• 争议的核心在于bootloader漏洞的存在价值。一方面是其对技术爱好者和自制软件社区的积极作用，另一方面是其对设备安全性的潜在威胁。这反映了在硬件漏洞问题上，功能扩展和安全性之间的平衡问题。

Magic Leap One Exploitation
Overview
This repository contains a (messy) implementation of my research of exploiting the Magic Leap One.
I will add writeups eventually, but for now, I just wanted to publish my code and give a simple explanation.
The
fastbooted
folder contains the code that runs on the Magic Leap console.
The
fastbootrs
folder contains a Rust implementation of a Fastboot client, and is the code that runs on the host.
SHA256(ML1 SBK)=25861920c4b750caaa851de7f92edbcf5fa3dfc396c54a871edff250ada8aa97
Vulns
This repository contains implementations of two vulns:
Code Execution in CBoot over Fastboot USB by smashing the stack in NVidia's SparseFS parser (
sparsehax
)
Overwriting CBoot in memory using an oversized
kernel-dtb
implementation on the storage to gain persistant code execution (
dtbhax
)
Both of these may effect more than just the ML1. I've not researched it much but there's a decent chance the
kernel-dtb
vuln can be used for persistence on the Autopilot units of certain cars using the TX2.
Usage
Warning: It's your responsibility if you brick your console.
You need a signed signature context (list of hashes with a small header and a signature) from a firmware update for your device (this is device unique), any partition works as long as it's for your device, I've been using the one from the system image. Place it in
fastbootrs/system-sparse-sig.bin
.
Inside the
fastbooted/payload
directory:
Copy
sparsehax.ld
to
ccplex.ld
Run
cargo build-usb-bin
Copy the generated
payload.bin
file to
fastbootrs/src/payload.bin
Put your ML1 console into Fastboot by powering it off, and holding the Vol-Down button whilst powering the console on.
Inside the
fastbootrs
directory:
Run
cargo run --release -- exploit
Success?
If these instructions aren't clear enough, this probably is not ready for you currently.

Coming soon

data.title: How the Sun Enterprise 10000 was born (2007)
data.author: robin_reala
data.article_summary: 《Sun Enterprise 10000的诞生》讲述了一群来自圣迭戈的工程师离职创业，致力于开发大规模并行计算机，使用Sparc处理器。他们经历多次收购与重组，最著名的是被Cray Research收购。在Cray领导下，他们开发了拥有64个Sparc处理器的CS6400，支持动态系统域和交替路径等功能。随后，Cray被SGI收购，SGI将该部门转售给Sun Microsystems，售价约5000万美元。Sun完成了该团队的后续项目——Ultra Enterprise Server 10000（也称Starfire）。该服务器具有更先进的动态重配置和更快的硬件架构，市场表现卓越，被誉为Sun最成功的收购之一。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Sun系统及其相关技术和历史评价

不同观点：
• **怀旧与个人经历**：[jasoneckert] 表达了对Sun系统的深厚感情，并提到即使尝试过使用“KonMari方法”清理旧设备，但依然舍不得丢弃。类似地，[trollied] 也提到对Sun大型设备（E10k/E15k）的热爱，并怀念过去在高性能计算中的乐趣。

• **技术挑战与维护经验**：[dmd] 分享了在1999年管理Sun系统时的技术挑战，尤其是系统需要持续维护以支持大量用户，并提到了一次通过物理撞击恢复系统响应的趣事。[eugenekay] 则提到在Mail.com工作时，使用了大量SCSI磁盘和Solaris服务器来支持前端SMTP服务。

• **技术转变与历史评价**：[ajross] 认为Sun的设备在发布时非常出色，但属于即将过时的架构，并将其与1980年代末期ECL大型机的命运相比较。他认为随着Web 2.0和云计算的兴起，这种设备逐渐被淘汰。[JSR_FDED] 则指出Sun通过收购Floating Point Systems等公司增强了竞争力，但也导致了SGI的战略失误。

• **设备性能与市场印象**：[nocoiner] 和 [jasongill] 都对Sun E10000 Starfire这一设备表达了高度赞誉，认为它是顶级性能和地位的象征。[jasongill] 特别提到拥有E10k的管理权限在当时是一种身份的象征。

• **设备失窃与安全问题**：[tverbeure] 分享了一个设备被盗的趣闻，提到公司购买的Sun设备在通过起重机运送并安装后不久即被盗走，怀疑是内部人员泄露了信息。

• **对管理层的批评与战略失误**：[hpcjoe] 批评了SGI管理层在将技术卖给Sun时的决策失误，并认为Bo Ewald的战略缺乏远见，导致了SGI的失败。

补充讨论：
• **技术规格与历史数据**：[znpy] 引用了技术文档，展示了Sun E10000的强大性能，包括其存储容量和CPU/内存配置，强调了其在1997年时的惊人技术水平。

• **技术社区与资源**：[bobmcnamara] 提到Cray-cyber.org曾经提供免费shell账户，显示了技术社区对Sun系统的支持和使用。

争议焦点：
• **Sun设备的历史地位与技术价值**：有些人认为Sun设备在当时代表了顶尖技术，但另一些人（如[ajross]）则认为这些设备属于过时的架构，最终被新的技术范式取代。

44020975.article_content:
How the Sun Enterprise 10000 was born
A group of
engineers in
San Diego left their jobs at well established
corporations (especially a large number of former
NCR employees) to form their own company. They set
out to build
massively parallel computers with
Sparc processors. The market they were targetting
has traditionally been a hard one, and they had a hard
time surviving. They were acquired by similar companies
and reshaped several times, most notably their second to
last acquisition by
Cray Research, Inc.. They were also joined with
several engineers in
Beaverton,
Oregon through these mergers.
Under
Cray's
leadership, they produced a machine with 64
Sparc processors called the
CS6400
(or more affectionately called the
SuperDragon since it was an implementation of Sun's
sun4d architecture, similar to what would be found
in a
SparcCenter 2000 computer from Sun). The CS6400
supported a feature called
Dynamic System Domains, meaning that its multiple
system boards could be electronically isolated into
distinct sets (called
domains), and that the partitioning could be changed
dynamically while separate instances of the operating
system were executing within each domain. Another
feature called
Alternate Pathing allowed SCSI and ethernet devices
to be virtualized on top of pairs of SCSI and ethernet
interface cards, allowing an operator to dynamically
repartition system boards or even physically remove
system boards from the
chassis without interrupting I/O services provided
to the end users.
A relationship was established between the engineers
who built the CS6400 and
Sun Microsystems because their large Sparc based
servers ran the
Solaris Operating Environment. (Well, along with a
few low level tweaks in the kernel to get
Solaris to work on the slightly different hardware,
and to support the Alternate Pathing feature and the
Dynamic Reconfiguration feature that allows the
kernel to release/claim resources as they're physically
detached/attached.)
When
Cray was purchased by
SGI, and while
SGI analyzed what it had just bought, it found this
quirky little division in
San Diego building things with Sparc processors and
working closely with
Sun Microsystems.
SGI didn't really want to keep the group,
considering that it clashed with the sorts of
technologies that SGI was already producing. So they
gladly sold the group off to Sun for about $50 million.
Sun liked what the engineers were doing and how their
computer systems worked, so it gladly acquired the
division just as it was about to complete its follow-on
to the CS6400: the Ultra Enterprise Server 10000 (also
known as the
Starfire).
Development was completed on the new machine under
Sun's leadership, and it took off in the marketplace
once the fine products from these brilliant engineers
were finally coupled with the vast resources of Sun's
marketing department. The Enterprise 10000 servers were
essentially a more modern and refined approach at what
the CS6400 was. The Enterprise 10000 had easier, more
reliable
Dynamic Reconfiguration. (Although, I'd advise using
the Solaris 7 or Solaris 8 versions of DR over the
Solaris 2.5.1 and Solaris 2.6 versions if possible; but
that's just my personal preference.) It also had faster
hardware based on a 16x16 crossbar implementation of
Sun's UPA architecture (sun4u, same as an Ultra-1,
except on a larger scale). The server was praised in the
computer industry for its success at scaling
SMP up to the largest number of processors ever
achieved, due in no small part to the amazing
ASICs that drive its interconnect with a remarkably
fast cache coherency snooping implementation. (All 64
processors can access any of the 64GB of memory in the
system with uniform performance measurements of
~12GBytes/sec of bandwidth and ~500ns of latency while
keeping their 8MB e-cache's coherent.)
Scott McNealy considers his company's acquisition of
the Enterprise 10000 and its engineers as the best deal
since
Microsoft bought
DOS. The acquired division was directly responsible
for several billion dollars in revenue during its first
year within Sun's ranks, not to mention the other
revenue associated with selling service and accessories
to go with all of that Enterprise 10000 hardware.

44020975.article_summary: 《Sun Enterprise 10000的诞生》讲述了一群来自圣迭戈的工程师离职创业，致力于开发大规模并行计算机，使用Sparc处理器。他们经历多次收购与重组，最著名的是被Cray Research收购。在Cray领导下，他们开发了拥有64个Sparc处理器的CS6400，支持动态系统域和交替路径等功能。随后，Cray被SGI收购，SGI将该部门转售给Sun Microsystems，售价约5000万美元。Sun完成了该团队的后续项目——Ultra Enterprise Server 10000（也称Starfire）。该服务器具有更先进的动态重配置和更快的硬件架构，市场表现卓越，被誉为Sun最成功的收购之一。

data.article_summary:
这篇文章介绍了多种基于折纸和材料变形的互动设计，包括：

1. **Flexagon**：通过材料的记忆弯曲，展示四帧循环故事。
2. **Hexaflexagon**：一种纸玩具，通过折叠展示循环故事，具有互动性和几何展示功能。
3. **5-Sided Collapsible Tube**与**Auxetic Metamaterial**：展示可折叠管和具有弹性的超材料。
4. **Miura-ori Fold**：一种可编程折叠方式，通过改变角度实现不同效果，常用于刚性材料如卫星太阳能板。
5. **Bistable Mechanism**：基于方形扭转模式，形成双稳态机制，像纸开关。
6. **Hexagonal Origami Flasher**：可折叠、可展开的结构。
7. **Rotating Cam with Arm**：展示机械工程原理，通过旋转凸轮产生动画效果。
8. **Two-Blind Reveal**：简化的双层结构，用于揭示内容。
9. **Linear to Rotary Movement**：拉动结构产生旋转运动。
10. **Percussive Object**：通过锯齿边产生不同节奏的打击声。
11. **Modified Waterbomb**：经典的水炸弹折痕图案，具有升降和展开的几何特性。

这些设计展示了折纸和材料在互动和机械工程中的创新应用。

no. 05
Miura-ori Fold
"Programmable" by deforming parts of the pattern
Try varying the angles
The Miura fold (ãã¦ã©æã Miura-ori) is a method of folding a flat surface such as a sheet of paper into a smaller area. The fold is named for its inventor, Japanese astrophysicist Koryo Miura.[1]
The crease patterns of the Miura fold form a tessellation of the surface by parallelograms. In one direction, the creases lie along straight lines, with each parallelogram forming the mirror reflection of its neighbor across each crease. In the other direction, the creases zigzag, and each parallelogram is the translation of its neighbor across the crease. Each of the zigzag paths of creases consists solely of mountain folds or of valley folds, with mountains alternating with valleys from one zigzag path to the next. Each of the straight paths of creases alternates between mountain and valley folds.[2]
The Miura fold is a form of rigid origami, meaning that the fold can be carried out by a continuous motion in which, at each step, each parallelogram is completely flat. This property allows it to be used to fold surfaces made of rigid materials. For instance, large solar panel arrays for space satellites in the Japanese space program have been Miura folded before launch and then spread out in space.[3][4] A folded Miura fold can be packed into a compact shape, its thickness reflecting only the thickness of the folded material. Folded material can be unpacked in one motion by pulling on its opposite ends, and likewise folded by pushing the two ends together. In the solar array application, this property reduces the number of motors required to unfold this shape, reducing weight and complexity. (Wikipedia)

• [bo0tzz] 仅提供了一个年份（2023），可能是在强调讨论的时间背景或表示对当前问题的关注，但没有展开具体观点。

补充讨论：
• PFAS污染的严重性和全球性影响是讨论的焦点，尤其是这些化学物质的难以降解性和对环境的长期影响。
• [flysand7] 对废物处理的创新性设想（如利用火箭技术）虽然目前看来不太现实，但反映了对当前废物处理技术局限性的反思和对未来解决方案的期待。
• 争议的焦点可能在于废物处理技术的可行性和经济性。虽然将废物送入太空听起来不切实际，但它揭示了对现有处理方法的不满和对更有效解决方案的需求。

整体来看，讨论围绕PFAS污染的严重性及其处理方案展开，涉及现有技术的局限性和未来可能的创新解决途径。

data.article_summary: Craft Basic 1.7.1是适用于Windows 95及以上系统的BASIC解释器，可用于学习编程、制作简单游戏、编写代码、执行复杂计算、显示图形、创建窗口和按钮、编写脚本等。它包含简单的命令来绘制位图和播放声音，并提供处理静态文本和按钮的功能，附带许多示例程序帮助用户入门。文件大小为269kB，可在Lucid Apogee官网和itch.io下载。系统要求为Windows 95及以上，支持多种Windows操作系统。近期更新包括对网络应用、位运算符、COLOR和LOCATE命令的支持，以及对例程的清理和新增。同时，发布了Express Calculator命令行科学计算器。

data.author: jandeboevrie
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了如何在Kubernetes上部署高可用的MQTT代理服务（使用Eclipse Mosquitto），通过使用Kubernetes的核心资源（如Deployments、Services、ConfigMaps、RBAC）以及Traefik IngressRouteTCP来实现外部流量暴露。该方案通过轻量级的自愈故障转移机制，在主代理失效时，可在5秒内将流量重定向到备用代理，从而减少宕机时间。该设置还利用MQTT桥接功能，确保主备代理之间的消息同步。与单Pod部署相比，这种方案在节点故障时能够显著降低恢复时间，并确保消息不丢失。客户端只需连接到同一个负载均衡服务端点，故障转移过程透明且迅速。文中提供了YAML配置示例，并说明了如何使用Traefik和k3s实现该方案。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Kubernetes和Mosquitto在高可用性（HA）场景下的使用及相关技术选择

不同观点：
• **zrail** 认为可以通过将两个Pod直接放入Kubernetes的Service中实现高可用性，因为Service会自动将流量路由到处于"Ready"状态的Pod。同时，zrail还提出可以使用headless service和init容器来设置Mosquitto的桥接机制，以实现主从Pod之间的数据同步。

• **andrewfromx** 质疑在处理长时TCP连接时，是否有必要在Kubernetes中增加额外的网络复杂性。他分享了自己在IoT公司中的实践经验，通过简单的轮询DNS来管理大量连接，而不使用Kubernetes或复杂的负载均衡器。他们自行开发了 broker，并通过Packer创建AMI来部署到EC2实例上。

• **oulipo** 提出是否可以使用更现代的实现（如EMQx）来更好地实现高可用性，暗示Mosquitto可能不是实现HA的最佳选择，并建议考虑其他技术方案。

补充讨论：
- **zrail** 对于Kubernetes的Service功能有一定了解，但对Mosquitto的具体配置存在疑问，特别是关于桥接机制的实现。
- **andrewfromx** 基于实际生产环境的经验，倾向于简化技术栈，避免Kubernetes带来的复杂性，并通过自建工具和基础架构来实现高可用性。
- **oulipo** 提出了替代技术方案的建议，认为现代的消息代理如EMQx可能更适合高可用性场景。

争议焦点：是否需要在Kubernetes中增加复杂的网络层来实现高可用性，或者是否有更简单或更现代的替代方案。
