data.title: Show HN: Python Simulator of David Deutsch’s "Constructor Theory of Time"
data.author: SandroG
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了一个基于David Deutsch构造理论（Constructor Theory）的Python模拟器。该项目通过代码实现了构造理论的核心概念，包括任务、构造器、不可逆任务和量子任务等，并展示了自复制和构造器引导的过程。主要功能包括ASCII可视化、连续动力学模拟、引力和电磁任务等。项目提供了演示脚本和单元测试，并欢迎社区贡献新功能和改进文档。该项目以教育为目的，基于MIT许可证发布。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕一个项目（可能与构造器理论相关）的能力、应用及理论背景的讨论。

不同观点：
• **amelius** 对项目的具体功能提出疑问，关注其是否能模拟氢原子及不同能量下两个氢原子的相互作用，表明对项目实际物理模拟能力的关注。
• **canvascritic** 对项目表示赞赏，认为它可以作为互动教科书用于教学或传播构造器理论，但也指出构造器理论在主流物理学中尚未获得稳固地位，提醒不熟悉的用户注意其中的炒作成分。同时，提出对量子引力和引力子任务缺乏可证伪物理模型的批评，认为这些内容可能只是数学化的角色扮演，但仍对项目表示支持，并提出通过可插拔后端来测试不同任务本体的建议。此外，还提出使用范畴论中的概念（如态射、函子、单子等）来改进项目建模方式的建议。
• **revskill** 对项目的用途提出直接质疑，表明对项目的目的和应用场景不明确。

补充讨论：
• **canvascritic** 强调了构造器理论与该项目之间的区别，指出批评针对的是构造器理论本身而非该具体项目。同时，详细阐述了如何利用范畴论来改进项目中的任务和构造器建模，显示出对项目技术实现的深入思考。
• 争议的焦点之一在于构造器理论在物理学中的地位以及该项目在多大程度上能够代表或实现该理论的实际应用。

constructor-theory-simulator
A
Python implementation
of David Deutsch’s Constructor Theory framework, exposing key concepts—from simple Tasks and branching substrates to quantum-gravity and electromagnetism—entirely in code. Includes a “universal constructor” that can bootstrap itself from a list of Tasks, demonstrating self-replication and the power of Constructor Theory.
“A demonstration of how constructor theory
could
be explored in code, not a high-precision physics engine. For the formal definitions, see David Deutsch and Chiara Marletto’s recent paper “
Constructor Theory of Time
” (May 13, 2025).
🚀 Features
Core framework
: Attributes, Substrates, Tasks, Constructors
Irreversible & quantum tasks
: Many-worlds branching, decoherence guards
Timers & Clocks
: Simulate proper-time, special/general relativity corrections
Fungibility & SwapConstructor
: Free exchange of identical substrates
ASCII visualizer
:
ascii_branch()
for quick text-based branch inspection
Continuous dynamics
: 1D & 2D substrates,
DynamicsTask
, RK4 & symplectic integrators
Coupling tasks
:
Gravitational two-body (1D)
Coulomb coupling (1D)
Lorentz-force (2D) for charged particles in a magnetic field
Quantum-Gravity & Electromagnetism
: Graviton & Photon emission/absorption Tasks
UniversalConstructor
: Bootstraps any list of Tasks into a working Constructor
Demo scripts
:
demo.py
– shows every constructor in action
bootstrap_demo.py
– elegant self-replication via the UniversalConstructor
🛠 Getting Started
Prerequisites
Python 3.8+
(Optional)
matplotlib
for phase-space plots
Installation
git clone https://github.com/gvelesandro/constructor-theory-simulator.git
cd
constructor-theory-simulator
Run Unit Tests
python -m unittest ct_tests.py
Run Demos
python demo.py
python bootstrap_demo.py
Note:

44024055.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了一个基于David Deutsch构造理论（Constructor Theory）的Python模拟器。该项目通过代码实现了构造理论的核心概念，包括任务、构造器、不可逆任务和量子任务等，并展示了自复制和构造器引导的过程。主要功能包括ASCII可视化、连续动力学模拟、引力和电磁任务等。项目提供了演示脚本和单元测试，并欢迎社区贡献新功能和改进文档。该项目以教育为目的，基于MIT许可证发布。

• **amelius** 对项目的具体功能提出疑问，关注其是否能模拟氢原子及不同能量下两个氢原子的相互作用，表明对项目实际物理模拟能力的关注。
• **canvascritic** 对项目表示赞赏，认为它可以作为互动教科书用于教学或传播构造器理论，但也指出构造器理论在主流物理学中尚未获得稳固地位，提醒不熟悉的用户注意其中的炒作成分。同时，提出对量子引力和引力子任务缺乏可证伪物理模型的批评，认为这些内容可能只是数学化的角色扮演，但仍对项目表示支持，并提出通过可插拔后端来测试不同任务本体的建议。此外，还提出使用范畴论中的概念（如态射、函子、单子等）来改进项目建模方式的建议。
• **revskill** 对项目的用途提出直接质疑，表明对项目的目的和应用场景不明确。

补充讨论：
• **canvascritic** 强调了构造器理论与该项目之间的区别，指出批评针对的是构造器理论本身而非该具体项目。同时，详细阐述了如何利用范畴论来改进项目中的任务和构造器建模，显示出对项目技术实现的深入思考。

data.article_summary: Vaev 是一个实验性网页浏览器引擎，主打快速、轻量和安全。它支持部分网页标准，包括多种显示类型（网格除外）、标准的 CSS 层叠行为、@page 规则分页和打印为 PDF、所有 CSS 单位（如百分比、var() 和 calc()），以及加载 HTML 和 XHTML 文档。网络功能仅支持基本的 HTTP 和文件协议。要试用 Vaev，需通过一系列命令安装依赖并克隆代码库。该项目采用 LGPL-3.0 许可，主要由几位开发者贡献。目前无正式发布版本。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于开发简化版浏览器的可行性和目标

不同观点：
• [khimaros] 认为应该为简化版浏览器（"smolweb"）建立一套一致的网页标准子集，以便同时兼容主流浏览器并为"smolweb"爱好者提供开发依据。他倾向于这种方法，而不是像Gemini这样的全新协议，因为这种方法保留了对主流浏览器的向后兼容性。

• [DarkmSparks] 提出将Android的WebView独立出来作为一个跨平台项目的想法，认为这可能是解决浏览器开发复杂性的一种方式，并表示有意查找是否已有类似项目。

• [abhisek] 对开发简化版浏览器的长期目标提出质疑，认为构建一个支持现代网络的浏览器工作量巨大，并询问除了学习之外，这种项目的最终目标是什么。

• [quibono] 表示愿意为相关项目贡献力量，特别希望有一个非Chromium的替代品来替代wkhtmltopdf，显示出对多样化浏览器工具的需求。

• [busymom0] 希望有一种仅渲染文本和链接的浏览器，不支持媒体文件（如图片、视频、音频等）。虽然知道有Lynx这样的文本浏览器，但认为一个非终端版的类似浏览器会更有吸引力。

data.title: Comparing Parallel Functional Array Languages: Programming and Performance
data.author: vok
data.article_summary: 这篇文章比较了五种并行函数式数组语言（Accelerate、APL、DaCe、Futhark、SaC）在编程便捷性和性能方面的表现。通过四个基准测试（N-body模拟、MultiGrid、Quickhull、Flash Attention），作者展示了函数式数组语言的表达能力和代码简洁性，这些代码能够自动生成多核和GPU可执行程序。实验在32核AMD EPYC 7313系统和NVIDIA A30 GPU上进行，结果表明成熟的函数式数组语言在性能上可与传统数值内核技术媲美，且更易于移植和优化。文章进一步分析了每种语言在不同基准和架构上的表现原因。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：编程语言在数值计算中的性能和功能特性，特别是与BLAS库的依赖以及函数式编程的纯度。

不同观点：
• teleforce认为D语言在数值计算方面表现出色，具有并行支持和高效的本地BLAS库（如Mir GLAS），其性能优于OpenBLAS和Eigen，并且具有类似Python的易用性。
• munchler关注编程语言在函数式编程方面的纯度，质疑包括D语言和APL在内的语言是否真正符合函数式编程的定义，尤其是关于是否允许状态突变和副作用。他认为如果数组内容被就地修改，就不应被视为函数式。
• yubblegum提到了Chapel语言，对其在HPC（高性能计算）领域的应用表示兴趣，并询问社区对Chapel的反馈。
• DrNosferatu用一句话概括Matlab为“可移植的APL”，暗示Matlab在某种程度上的简化和普及性。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中提到了多个编程语言，包括D语言、APL、Chapel和Matlab，涉及它们在数值计算和高性能计算中的应用和特性。
• teleforce提供了具体的性能比较数据，引用了2016年的基准测试结果，以支持其对D语言性能的评价。
• munchler的评论引发了关于函数式编程纯度的争议，特别是关于状态突变和副作用在实际应用中的影响。
• yubblegum对Chapel语言的兴趣引出了对HPC领域编程语言选择的更广泛讨论。
• DrNosferatu的评论虽然简短，但提供了一种对Matlab和APL之间关系的有趣视角。

View PDF
Abstract:
Parallel functional array languages are an emerging class of programming languages that promise to combine low-effort parallel programming with good performance and performance portability. We systematically compare the designs and implementations of five different functional array languages: Accelerate, APL, DaCe, Futhark, and SaC. We demonstrate the expressiveness of functional array programming by means of four challenging benchmarks, namely N-body simulation, MultiGrid, Quickhull, and Flash Attention. These benchmarks represent a range of application domains and parallel computational models. We argue that the functional array code is much shorter and more comprehensible than the hand-optimized baseline implementations because it omits architecture-specific aspects. Instead, the language implementations generate both multicore and GPU executables from a single source code base. Hence, we further argue that functional array code could more easily be ported to, and optimized for, new parallel architectures than conventional implementations of numerical kernels. We demonstrate this potential by reporting the performance of the five parallel functional array languages on a total of 39 instances of the four benchmarks on both a 32-core AMD EPYC 7313 multicore system and on an NVIDIA A30 GPU. We explore in-depth why each language performs well or not so well on each benchmark and architecture. We argue that the results demonstrate that mature functional array languages have the potential to deliver performance competitive with the best available conventional techniques.

data.author: rbanffy
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一家开放源代码机器人公司，致力于加速实现大规模机器人应用，并确保其对人类有益、可访问和可审计。公司提供多款通用人形机器人（如K-Bot、Z-Bot、M-Bot），价格从999美元到15,999美元不等，现已开放预订。其机器人技术栈包括硬件、软件和机器学习，集成良好，支持快速部署物理AI。K-Lang语言、K-Sim强化学习框架及K-OS操作系统等工具帮助开发者高效创建、测试和部署机器人应用。所有代码均为开源，并支持模拟到现实的无缝转移。公司已完成六代机器人开发，并与学术界（如斯坦福大学）合作推广。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：针对一个机器人项目的不同观点和讨论

不同观点：
• OsrsNeedsf2P认为该机器人项目有潜力，特别是在实际生活中的应用（如做家务），但目前实现的效果不佳，尤其是机器人在执行器打滑后无法识别自身位置，导致不稳定。
• dang提到之前可能有人分享过相关内容，但自己无法进行太多管理操作，并询问是否有人可以提供更多链接信息，希望有更多讨论。
• v9v对项目开源设计表示质疑，认为项目网站缺乏硬件细节，GitHub仓库和文档均为空白，要求更多具体硬件信息。
• awongh关注价格问题，认为该机器人比预期的便宜，并询问是否存在其他价格相似的 humanoid 机器人。
• canvascritic对项目宣传持怀疑态度，认为其宣传类似于早期DeepMind和Tesla的AI宣传。虽然项目声称有突破性进展，但缺少实际的基准测试来验证其技术实力。同时指出，项目如果真的成功，其核心可能在于RL基础设施，而非机器人本身。
• paulsutter从工业应用角度出发，认为该项目可以作为大公司难以接触的替代方案，计划深入研究并帮助推动现有技术的发展。

补充讨论：
• whatever1对项目团队的工作态度和实际执行能力提出质疑，讽刺他们一边声称努力工作，一边却向外界寻求帮助设计RL奖励函数。
• 争议的焦点在于该机器人项目的实际可行性和技术细节的透明度，尤其是硬件实现和宣传内容的真实性。

data.title: Hyper Typing
data.author: azhenley
data.article_summary:
本文讨论了TypeScript类型系统中的一个固有权衡：更严格的类型更安全，但往往更复杂。作者提出一种称为“过度类型化”（hyper-typing）的现象，即一些库为了追求完美的类型安全，导致类型过于复杂，难以理解，产生晦涩的错误信息，甚至引发不安全的变通方法。作者认为，简单的类型或类型生成通常能带来更实用和愉快的开发体验，尽管它们不是“完美”的。

例如，宽松的类型定义容易理解但不够安全，而严格的类型定义如使用泛型和`keyof`可以提供编译时保障，却增加了复杂性。以TanStack Form库为例，虽然其类型安全和自动完成功能强大，但其类型定义复杂难懂，错误信息难以解读。

过度类型化的缺点包括：类型定义文件格式不佳、类型难以理解，以及因难以使用而导致的不安全变通方法。作者建议在类型严格性和可理解性之间找到平衡。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：TypeScript中复杂类型的使用及其优缺点

不同观点：
• jasonthorsness认为，完全类型的库是非常有用的，问题通常出在API设计不合理，而不是类型本身。复杂的API无论是否有类型注解都会很难用。
• sberens建议IDE应增加更多关于类型的工具功能，例如展开类型层次，以便更容易理解复杂类型。
• KevinMS担忧TypeScript的复杂类型会导致其声誉受损，最终可能像Perl一样被抛弃。
• CapsAdmin指出，复杂类型通常反映了底层代码的复杂性，尤其是在处理JavaScript的动态特性时，这种现象更加明显。
• codethief反对Astro框架生成的类型，认为这些类型带来了很多问题和错误。
• chris_armstrong认为TypeScript允许复杂类型定义是其问题的根源，建议使用更简单的子集类型和代码生成工具来提高可读性。
• nine_k认为，复杂和嵌套的类型通常是缺乏抽象的结果，应该通过提取中间类型来简化。
• Waterluvian喜欢模板类型和点标记路径，但希望TypeScript能更直观地表达数值范围。
• skrebbel支持使用"Hyper Typing"这一术语来描述过度设计的类型安全。
• pscanf作为原文作者，好奇其他人是否有类似的经历或认为复杂类型是值得的。
• codr7以自身经验说明过度类型设计并不总是好的，特别是在数据库类型的编码中。
• ninetyninenine不同意复杂类型无用，认为通过合理命名和使用别名可以简化复杂类型。
• coryvirok强力支持强类型，认为其在性能优化、减少错误路径和降低漏洞风险方面有显著优势。
• arcfour认为引入TypeScript带来了更多类型问题，更倾向于简单的JSDoc类型注解。

补充讨论：
• BarryGuff对讨论的主题有误解，以为是关于高速打字。
• 争议的焦点在于复杂类型的必要性和实用性，一些开发者认为复杂类型提供了更多安全性和优化机会，而另一些开发者则认为复杂类型增加了理解和使用的难度。

44024173.article_content:
In this article, I talk about an inherent trade-off in TypeScript's type
system: stricter types are safer, but often more complex. I describe a
phenomenon I call "hyper-typing", where libraries - in pursuit of perfect type
safety - end up with overly complex types that are hard-to-understand, produce
cryptic errors, and paradoxically even lead to unsafe workarounds.
I argue that simpler types, or even type generation, often lead to a more
practical and enjoyable developer experience despite being less "perfect".
TypeScript’s type system is
gradual
: when describing a JavaScript value with
TypeScript, you can be more or less accurate, ranging from saying that the value
could be anything (
any
), to describing in absolute detail what the value is
under different conditions.
Consider for example this function which prints the property of an object - if
it exists:
function
printProperty
(
obj
,
key
)
{
if
(
typeof
obj
===
"object"
&&
obj
!==
null
&&
Object.
hasOwn
(obj,
key))
{
console.
log
(obj[key]);
}
}
We can type it in a
loose
way as follows:
function
printProperty
(
obj
:
any
,
key
:
string
)
{
if
(
typeof
obj
===
"object"
&&
obj
!==
null
&&
Object.
hasOwn
(obj,
key))
{
console.
log
(obj[key]);
}
}
But we can also be more
strict
, requiring
obj
to be an object and
key
to
be one of its properties:
function
printProperty
<
Obj
extends
object
>(
obj
:
Obj
,
key
:
keyof
Obj
)
{
console.
log
(obj[key]);
}
The strictness even allows us to remove the
if
check inside the function,
since now TypeScript gives us the compile-time guarantee that
obj
will always
have property
key
:
//
Passing
in
a
non-existing
property
gives
an
error.
printProperty
({
a:
"a"
},
"b"
);
Argument of type '"b"' is not assignable to parameter of type '"a"'.
Having this additional guarantee is obviously desirable, but it comes at the
expense of making the type definition more complex. Not much in this case - the
type is still very understandable - but it reveals an inherent trade-off. Where
should we draw the line?
Hyper-Typing
Lately I’ve been trying out a few libraries that - in pursuit of perfect type
safety - make their typings so complex that it makes them almost unusable, in my
opinion. I call this approach
hyper-typing
, and I worry it’s becoming a trend
in the TypeScript ecosystem.
I get why, actually. I myself am often a
hyper-typer
! It’s a slippery slope:
“If I add this type constraint then the caller will get an error in this
particular case”. “I can make this function infer this type here so the caller
will get the correct type hint there”.
At the bottom of the slope you get to a place where yes, things work, and they
might also look good for the caller -
in the happy case
. The resulting types,
however, are a complex mess, and the compilation errors produced when the caller
deviates from the happy path are walls of inscrutable text.
An Example: TanStack Form
TanStack Form is the new kid on the block of form libraries. It pushes heavily
on type-safety, promising “first-class TypeScript support with outstanding
autocompletion” for a “smoother development experience”.
What the library accomplishes is honestly impressive. Just give it the default
values of your form and you’re set: now for every form field you define - no
matter how deeply nested - you get the correct type when you read or write its
value, when you do validation, etc.
Don’t look at how the sausage is made, though: you won’t even understand it.
Take
the simple example from TanStack Form’s documentation
.
Use the interactive sandbox and try to check what’s the shape of a field’s
meta
property (or any other library value, really). Here’s what you’ll see:
The
FieldMeta
type has 17 (!) generic parameters and is the intersection of
two types - each taking the same 17 generics - which is where you eventually
find its properties defined.
To be fair, after re-formatting the type definition file and staring at it for a
couple of minutes, I do start to understand what’s going on. For the
FieldMeta
type in particular there’s nothing too obscure, but I can’t help but feel that
this undoubtedly clever and accurate type definition is not actually
helping
me as a user of the library.
Cons of Hyper-Typing
TanStack Form is one example of a hyper-typing library, but as I said, lately
I’ve encountered others that follow a similar approach and leave me with similar
issues:
Badly-formatted type definition files
. This is technically TypeScript’s
fault, but I guess the issue is not apparent until the typings become very
complex. It should be easy to fix, though, just by running the files through
prettier.
Difficult to understand types
. I agree that they’re safer and more
accurate, but that’s not very useful if I don’t understand what they’re
actually describing.
Unsafe workarounds
. Getting into situations where I need to explicitly
define a type is inevitable, and when the library types are so difficult to
understand and use, I often end up resorting to casting things
as any
,
losing

data.title: The Fall of Roam
data.author: ingve
data.article_summary: 本文由Dan Shipper撰写，探讨了他对Roam这款笔记工具的体验变化。Roam曾因其双向链接功能风靡一时，让用户可以轻松构建高度网络化的笔记系统。然而，作者发现，随着时间推移，他很少 revisit 这些链接，笔记系统变得像一个“垃圾场”，而且每次记笔记时都会困扰于“该放哪儿”的问题。Roam的 product velocity 慢、移动端体验差以及社区问题等因素，也让作者不再频繁使用Roam。尽管Roam的设计初衷是解决笔记组织问题，但实际效果不如预期，最终导致作者放弃了它。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Roam等笔记工具的优缺点及个人知识管理方法

不同观点：

The Fall of Roam
I don’t use Roam anymore. Why?
Dan Shipper
February 12, 2022
Link copied
283
6
I used to use
Roam
every day, but I don’t use it much anymore. Based on what I can see on Twitter, and a casual survey of friends, I don’t think I’m alone.
A year ago, the idea of networking our notes with bi-directional links became the biggest thing in the
tools
for thought space since Vannevar Bush described the
memex
. Top-down hierarchies and tag systems became the
pet explanation
du jour for everything that was wrong with
note-taking
. So we all hustled on to the Double-Bracket Express determined to build our own networked knowledge graphs. But where did we actually go? At least for me—and most of the people I know—we got a garbage dump full of crufty links and pieces of text we hardly ever revisit. And we feel guilty and sad about it.
(It is a very appealing looking garbage dump, however.)
There are probably a host of reasons why this happened: Roam’s product velocity seems to be incredibly slow, there still isn’t really a good mobile experience, they’ve had well-documented community issues—the list goes on.
But there’s one main reason that I don’t use it anymore:
When I write my notes the thought, ‘Where am I going to put this?
’
plagues me every time. It’s a direct and immediate pain. And it sometimes gets in the way of me even taking notes at all. I have this sensation many times a day and it’s deeply uncomfortable.
Roam’s job was to get rid of that pain. And it did—for a while. But now it’s back.
.    .    .
The core idea that caught on with Roam is the concept of a bidirectional link. Previous note-taking systems allowed linking in only one direction: you could link from one note to another, but the note being linked to had no automatic link back to the original note.
Bi-directional linking, by contrast, creates a link from the first note to the second, and from the second to the first automatically. Roam made this extremely easy to accomplish—just by typing pieces of your notes in [[ brackets ]] you could link between notes, and even create new ones if the note you were linking to didn’t already exist.
The idea was to create a highly-networked system of notes with lots of links between them. By doing so, you could increase serendipitous encounters with old notes, and decrease your risk of losing a note, and generally get more out of the whole note-taking experience, or indeed life itself:
Adam Keesling
@adam_keesling
I've been trying
@RoamResearch
for a week now
I was not expecting this, but it's completely changed my interactions with the entire *world*
Quick review 👇
November 19th 2019, 1:54pm EST
110
Retweets
952
Likes
I believed that if I used it, I’d learn more from my experiences because I wouldn’t forget them. I’d take away more lessons from the books I’d read because I’d always have them close at hand. I’d make better decisions, produce better writing, and maybe my hair would even start to look as lustrous as Conor’s.
(Side-by-side comparison. How am I doing on the hair part?)
There’s a ton of intelligence and deep thought behind Roam’s design. But did it actually work for me?
Not really. If I plotted out the percent of my time writing bidirectional links vs. actually looking at my notes and clicking through the links in them, this is what I estimate it would look like:
It turns out that I am rarely in a position, while writing or thinking, where I want to glance through lots of old notes as a way to figure out what to say or do. Mostly that feels like sifting through stale garbage.
My most common behavior is to Actually Write the Notes. That’s why Roam needs to help me with the thought, ‘I don’t know where to put this.
’
If it does that well, it makes the vast majority of my time spent in the app a breeze. If it does that poorly, it makes my experience so painful that I want to switch systems.
The genius of bi-directional linking is that when I first started to use it, the neurotic hamster in my head decided to turn down the volume knob on the ‘Where should I put this?
’
question.
Why? Bidirectional linking is a very good story. Roam’s job is to make me believe that if I just surround pieces of my notes like this [[ ]] I won’t really have to worry about finding the note again. It’s now networked! The need to take notes far outstripped the need to review them (see: graph above), so Roam solved my problem.
After some time though, reality started to sink in. ‘I am not really going back through all of these notes as often as I thought I would.
’
My next automatic assumption is that if they were just organized better I might go through them more. And so, the question starts t

data.title: Yahtzeeql – Yahtzee solver that's mostly SQL
data.author: skadamat
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了一个主要使用SQL实现的Yahtzee游戏求解器（Yahtzeeql）。该项目包含多个策略来模拟游戏过程，包括随机选择、贪婪算法、全力争取Yahtzee等。用户可以通过命令行运行模拟，指定策略和游戏次数，还可以选择交互模式和显示结果图表。项目使用概率表（由`build_prob_db.py`生成并存储于SQLite数据库中）来优化决策，数据库包含不同掷骰结果的得分和转移概率。最终结果显示不同策略的平均得分，其中基于概率和难度优化的策略表现最佳，得分为89.5。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Yahtzee游戏的优化与解决方法

不同观点：
• [canvascritic] 认为可以通过SQL joins的巧妙运用来暴力搜索一个有限空间内的2-ply MDP（马尔可夫决策过程），并指出使用预计算的转移/得分表来模拟和优化轮流游戏是经典的强化学习方法。他还建议通过训练一个策略网络来近似SQL策略，从而将暴力搜索策略提炼为快速且可微的策略，并提出可以加入针对人类心理的优化，例如考虑人们更喜欢获得Yahtzee而非其他分数组合。

• [BarryGuff] 则认为Yahtzee完全依赖于骰子投掷的随机运气，不可能被"解决"。他否认了通过计算或策略来优化游戏结果的可能性。

补充讨论：
• [canvascritic] 强调了该方法作为学习预期值优化的教学工具对学生的价值，并提出了进一步优化策略的可能性，如加入效用函数。

• [BarryGuff] 的观点较为单一，集中于否定任何通过计算解决Yahtzee的可能性，但没有提出具体的论据或例子支持这一观点。

争议焦点：Yahtzee是否可以通过计算和策略优化来“解决”，还是完全依赖于运气。

Yahtzeeql - Yahtzee solver that's mostly SQL
Setup
python3 -m venv yahtzee-venv
source yahtzee-venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
./test.sh
You should see outputs for each strategy, in ascending order by goodness
Usage
python3 yahtzee.py --strategy <strategy> --runs <runs> [--interactive] [--show-plot]
Where
strategy
is one of:
random
- just keep the dice you're given, and pick a random category
random_greedy
- just keep the dice you're given, and pick the category that gives the highest score
all_yahtzee
- Do everything possible to get a Yahtzee every turn
prob
- Use probability tables to maximize the fraction of points you earn
prob_with_difficulty
- Use probability tables to maximize the fraction of points you earn, considering the difficulty of each category
--runs
is the number of games to simulate
--interactive
will show you the dice and ask you to pick a category for each turn
--show-plot
will show you a plot of the score distribution
Probabilty tables
build_prob_db.py
generates a sqlite database with a few tables:
all_rolls
- All rolls of 5 dice, with dice sorted in ascending order
roll_transitions
- The probability of transitioning from one roll to another, while keeping some subset of the first roll
level0
- For each roll, its score in each category, reprersented as a fraction of the maximum possible score in that category, and the raw score
level1
- For each roll, the expected value of each roll/keep/strategy combination, based on the sum of the expected values of each possible next roll from the level1 table
Results
random
- 84.5
random_greedy
- 86.5
all_yahtzee
- 87.5
prob
- 88.5
prob_with_difficulty
- 89.5

data.title: Show HN: Stack Error – ergonomic error handling for Rust
data.author: garrinm
data.article_summary:
`Stack Error` 是一个用于 Rust 的错误处理库，旨在降低设计错误处理方案的初期成本，帮助开发者专注于编写高质量的库和应用程序。它有三大目标：提供类似 `anyhow` 的易用性，创建有助于调试的详细错误信息，并提供便于运行时错误处理的类型化数据。

该库通过宏简化常见操作，自动附加文件名和行号信息，生成易于理解的错误消息。它还支持自定义错误类型和错误代码，兼容更广泛的 Rust 生态系统。与 `anyhow` 相比，`Stack Error` 提供了更清晰的错误信息和上下文，便于调试；而与 `thiserror` 相比，它填补了 `anyhow` 和 `thiserror` 之间的空白，提供了更灵活的错误处理方案。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Rust中错误处理和位置追踪的实现方式，特别是`StackError`宏与其它解决方案的比较。

不同观点：
• [lilyball] 认为如果宏的主要目的是获取文件和行号信息，可以通过使用`#[track_caller]`和`std::panic::Location`来替代宏。具体实现上，他们建议在`StackError`中添加一个带有`#[track_caller]`的函数，以便获取位置信息，并指出如果只需要静态字符串，直接使用函数会更简洁。此外，他们提到在`Display`实现中不应包含错误的来源信息，以避免重复输出，但可以在`Debug`实现中打印来源信息。

• [shepmaster] 对`StackError`库表示兴趣，并提到自己的库SNAFU，询问`StackError`与SNAFU的区别，希望了解更多细节。

• [tevon] 对`StackError`表示赞赏，并询问在编译后的二进制文件中如何追踪文件名和行号。他们提到在JavaScript中需要source-map来处理压缩代码的映射，想知道Rust中是如何实现的。

• [rhabarba] 表示虽然更喜欢Anyhow解决方案，但欣赏`StackError`的实现方法，暗示不同工具有不同的适用场景和个人偏好。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中提到了多种错误处理库的比较，包括`StackError`、SNAFU和Anyhow，反映出Rust社区中对错误处理的多样化需求和偏好。

• 对于文件和行号的追踪，[lilyball] 提供的`#[track_caller]`和`std::panic::Location`方案是一个值得注意的技术细节，显示了Rust中通过标准库功能实现位置追踪的可行性。

• [tevon] 的问题引出了Rust编译后二进制文件中位置信息的追踪机制，这一技术细节对于不熟悉Rust内部机制的开发者来说是一个重要的学习点。

44023471.article_summary:
`Stack Error` 是一个用于 Rust 的错误处理库，旨在降低设计错误处理方案的初期成本，帮助开发者专注于编写高质量的库和应用程序。它有三大目标：提供类似 `anyhow` 的易用性，创建有助于调试的详细错误信息，并提供便于运行时错误处理的类型化数据。

该库通过宏简化常见操作，自动附加文件名和行号信息，生成易于理解的错误消息。它还支持自定义错误类型和错误代码，兼容更广泛的 Rust 生态系统。与 `anyhow` 相比，`Stack Error` 提供了更清晰的错误信息和上下文，便于调试；而与 `thiserror` 相比，它填补了 `anyhow` 和 `thiserror` 之间的空白，提供了更灵活的错误处理方案。

data.title: What Is This Thing Called Swing?
data.author: Tomte
data.article_summary:
文章探讨了爵士乐中“摇摆感”（swing feel）的核心要素，特别是同步性和微时差偏差（microtiming deviations, MTDs）的作用。尽管“摇摆感”被认为是爵士乐表演的 essential 元素，但其具体构成仍然不明确。文章提到，目前唯一明确的是八分音符的不均等划分，即“摇摆比率”（swing ratio）。然而，仅靠这一比率不足以解释摇摆感，计算机生成的音乐即使有合适的摇摆比率，爵士乐手仍觉得缺乏摇摆感。

文章进一步讨论了微时差偏差是否是摇摆感的关键因素。通过实验，研究者发现某些系统性的微时差偏差确实对摇摆感有积极影响，而随机偏差则没有。研究采用操作性定义，邀请专业爵士乐手评估不同版本的演奏，最终证明系统性微时差偏差对摇摆感有实质贡献。

44023786.article_content:
What is This Thing Called Swing?
The Role of Synchronization for the Swing Feel in Jazz
Jazz must swing - jazz musicians agree on that. However, even a century after the beginnings of jazz, there is still no general agreement what exactly constitutes the swing feel. With a dedicated experiment and data analyses on more than 450 well-known jazz solos, we have tried to unravel some secrets of swing.
(For more details, see C. Nelias et al. Downbeat delays are a key component of the swing feel in jazz
[1]
).
"It Don't Mean a Thing, If It Ain't Got That Swing"
The swing feel is one of the most salient features of jazz music and is considered an essential ingredient of jazz performances, as reflected e.g. in the title of Duke Ellington's jazz standard "It Don't Mean a Thing, If It Ain't Got That Swing". The notion of swing was introduced by jazz musicians to denote a specific performance style they considered essential for jazz. Yet despite its central role it is still unclear what are the main musical and psychoacoustical constituents of the swing feel. It was even argued in the past that "you can feel it but you just can’t explain it"
[2]
, or similarly, according to The New Harvard Dictionary of Music, that swing is "an intangible rhythmic momentum in jazz ... swing deﬁes analysis"
[3]
.
Even today, there is still no consensus among jazz musicians as to which musical details (apart from the "swung notes") create the swing feel. This becomes apparent from the following
word cloud
, which summarizes the various answers that jazz musicians gave us to this question in an earlier project.
Among the possible components of swing only one is established unambiguously so far, the conspicuous unequal subdivision of quarter notes into long and short eighth notes ("swung notes"). It is measured by the so-called swing ratio, i.e., the length ratio of consecutive long and short eighth notes that are known as downbeats and offbeats.
Interactive tool: What are downbeats, offbeats, and swing ratio?
Downbeat refers to the ﬁrst eighth of a quarter note, offbeat to the second eighth.
Click here
for our interactive tool with audio examples demonstrating downbeats and offbeats. It also allows you to explore and experience different swing ratios.
This alternation of downbeats and offbeats played at unequal lengths is an easily perceivable and generally accepted prerequisite of swing, which is not sufficient, however. Listening to computer-generated jazz music that was “swingiﬁed” by merely implementing a suitable swing ratio, it is obvious to jazz musicians that there must be other components. But which are these components, and which ones are important?
Microtiming deviations as a cause of swing?
It has long been speculated that so-called microtiming deviations (MTDs) play the dominant role for the swing feel, besides accentuation, syncopation, and phrasing. However, while the importance of the swing ratio is generally accepted, the role of rhythmic microtiming deviations has been a subject of controversy for many decades. Various authors have emphasized the importance of participatory discrepancies; i.e. "little discrepancies within a jazz drummer’s beat, between bass and drums, between rhythm section and soloists, that create ’swing’ and invite us to participate"
[4]
. Others contested their inﬂuence and rather stressed the importance of rhythmic accuracy. Many of these claims were based on analyses of extracts from individual jazz musicians, which may explain the origin of the controversial claims, as MTDs are not used equally by all musicians. It is not clear, however, that MTDs - even if they occur - are speciﬁcally related to and enhance the swing feel. Is there a way to prove that MTDs do contribute substantially to the swing feel?
If jazz musicians can feel it, but not explain it precisely, we should be able to characterize the role of microtiming deviations by having experienced jazz musicians evaluate recordings in which we manipulated the microtiming in various ways. Adopting an operational deﬁnition of swing (i.e., the performance of a piece swings if it is judged as swinging by expert listeners) and using an experimental approach, we were able to clarify the controversy and to rigorously demonstrate a positive effect of certain systematic MTDs on swing. In a preceding study of our research group we found that involuntary random MTDs did not enhance swing [5], as quantized versions (without MTDs) of 12 different jazz pieces were rated highest by listeners. The question remained open, whether systematic MTDs play a role for the swing feel.

文章探讨了爵士乐中“摇摆感”（swing feel）的核心要素，特别是同步性和微时差偏差（microtiming deviations, MTDs）的作用。尽管“摇摆感”被认为是爵士乐表演的 essential 元素，但其具体构成仍然不明确。文章提到，目前唯一明确的是八分音符的不均等划分，即“摇摆比率”（swing ratio）。然而，仅靠这一比率不足以解释摇摆感，计算机生成的音乐即使有合适的摇摆比率，爵士乐手仍觉得缺乏摇摆感。

文章进一步讨论了微时差偏差是否是摇摆感的关键因素。通过实验，研究者发现某些系统性的微时差偏差确实对摇摆感有积极影响，而随机偏差则没有。研究采用操作性定义，邀请专业爵士乐手评估不同版本的演奏，最终证明系统性微时差偏差对摇摆感有实质贡献。

data.title: If nothing is curated, how do we find things
data.author: nivethan
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了在信息过载的时代，缺乏有效策展机制导致人们难以找到有价值的内容。作者以Bjork推广新电影《Cornucopia》为例，指出社交媒体散布信息的方式让寻找准确信息变得混乱和耗时。文章反思了过去由专业策展人和评论家筛选内容的便利，如通过电台、电视节目和杂志发现新音乐和电影。如今，依赖算法推荐的内容使用户困在信息茧房中，难以接触到多样化的艺术作品。作者呼吁重拾策展和评论的重要性，以帮助人们在海量信息中找到值得关注的内容，减轻精神上的疲惫感。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：文化内容的发现与策展机制的变化及其影响

不同观点：
• jedberg认为，过去的电台音乐总监筛选出的歌曲创造了共享的文化体验，而现在通过算法推荐的音乐让人感觉孤独，缺乏共同的文化体验。
• romankolpak强调，过去的音乐发现是通过社区和人际关系进行的，而现在的算法推荐缺乏人与人之间的联系和信任。
• lapcat则对专业评论家和策展的需求持矛盾态度，认为可以通过公共图书馆等随机方式发现内容，不一定需要依赖策展。
• arguflow指出，像Hacker News这样的平台提供了一种集体共识的体验，使得内容发现具有一定的共享性。
• protocolture认为好的策展非常棒，但目前的流媒体平台算法不够完善，导致推荐内容质量下降。
• paleotrope提出，当前文化内容的数量远超过去，算法虽然试图解决这个问题，但匹配度不高。
• zoomTo125建议通过分类和浏览最新或热门内容来发现新事物，但认为平台往往无法正确实现这一简单概念。
• robust-cactus指出，社交媒体巨头实际上在进行更多的策展，只是这种方式更加不透明。
• chowells认为，虽然策展有价值，但某些非常优秀的内容即使没有策展也能通过口碑传播被发现。
• tacke2000对比了过去和现在在产品选择上的信息过载问题，质疑过去是否真的更好。
• gorfian_robot建议通过特定的在线电台获取策展体验。
• fellowniusmonk批评当前的UI和平台剥夺了自我探索和发现的乐趣，呼吁更多开放源平台。
• WarOnPrivacy提出如何在充满噪音的信息环境中找到有用的策展内容。
• Papazsazsa认为策展是人类特有的行为，无法被AGI/ASI替代。
• monatron指出，当前的工具能够很好地聚合和分类信息，但这些工具多由大型科技公司提供，不过也有表现良好的开源版本。

补充讨论：
- 发现新音乐、新内容的方式已经从过去的电台和社区推荐转变为依赖算法和流媒体平台。
- 共享文化体验的缺失是许多人关注的一个重要问题，过去因为媒体和内容传播方式的限制，人们有更多的共同文化话题。
- 算法推荐虽然能提供个性化内容，但缺乏人际信任和社区归属感。
- 公共图书馆等传统方式仍然被一些人用来随机发现新内容。
- 开放源平台和工具被认为是解决当前策展问题的一种可能途径。

争议焦点：
- 策展的必要性及其在现代信息环境中的实现方式。
- 算法推荐与人类策展之间的优劣对比。
- 信息过载和内容发现效率的问题。

44015144.article_content:
If nothing is curated, how do we find things?
May 15, 2025
Bjork is currently promoting a new concert film being released called
Cornucopia
. She's been releasing new photoshoots and interviews almost every day for the past two weeks. For a musician who normally goes into hiding and only emerges when it's time to promote something, it's been a pretty exciting time to be a fan. However, all the information being put out, promoted on social media and reposted on places like Reddit, have all been a little confusing.
I saw a post from someone on Reddit asking to "explain to me like I'm five" what exactly is being released and what is it. Someone did reply to them with information, but the comment thread turned into a short argument as another commenter disagreed that the film would have a documentary attached to it. "Where did you get that info from?" a commenter asked. "I think I saw it somewhere in another interview that I translated into English," they replied, "but I might have gotten that wrong."
While reading this I thought, "It's times like these where an old-fashioned website would come in handy." Because, quite frankly, it would.
1
As convenient as social media is, it scatters the information like bread being fed to ducks. You then have to hunt around for the info or hope the magical algorithm gods read your mind and guide the information to you.
I always felt like social media creates an illusion of convenience. Think of how much time it takes to stay on top of things. To stay on top of music or film. Think of how much time it takes these days, how much hunting you have to do. Although technology has made information vast and reachable, it's also turned the entire internet into a sludge pile. And now, instead of relying on professional curators to sort through things for us, now
we
have to do the sorting.
Think of the old days. When I was a kid, I lived in a podunk, suburban town in the middle of nowhere. It wasn't a major city or even a major state, but I was able to quite easily stay on top of everything pop culture related, even things that weren't mainstream or even super popular in my country.
I discovered interesting music like Aphex Twin, Squarepusher, Portishead, Tricky, Orbital, Takako Minekawa, Hooverphonic, Poe, Veruca Salt all from sporadically listening to one college radio station in my hometown and, once a week, watching one music program on MTV (usually
120 Minutes
or
AMP
). Then, once a month, I would sometimes flip through a music magazine while at the hair salon (usually
Rolling Stone
or
Spin
). And that was literally it.
Same with movies. Once a week I would watch
Ebert and Roeper
, who would discuss and review all the releases of that week, including indie and foreign ones. I would also sometimes flip through film magazines or randomly stumble across something cool being aired on the IFC channel or Bravo
2
. That was how I discovered indie films like
Welcome to the Dollhouse
and
Run, Lola, Run
. I was a "cool," knowledgeable cultural teen with next to no Internet access.
The rise of social media has killed the art of curation because, these days, things are rarely curated. Criticism is dead (with Fantano
3
being the one exception) and Gen Alpha doesn't know how to find music through anything but TikTok. Relying on algorithms puts way too much power in technology's hands. And algorithms can only predict content that you've seen before. It'll never surprise you with something different. It keeps you in a little bubble. Oh, you like shoegaze? Well, that's all the algorithm is going to give you until you intentionally start listening to something else.
It makes art (music, film, tv, etc.) seem like one big sludge pile. It makes it feel vast and exhausting, like an endless list of things that you'll never get to the end of. I've been noticing this sentiment with society, this feeling of always being mentally exhausted. How many times have we had a discussion with a friend who was recommending a show and our response was, "Oh yeah, I'll have to see it, but my list of shows is so long!" The reality is we're not going to watch it because we feel like we have no time to get through everything and we don't fully trust other people's recommendations.
And that's where curation comes in. We need critics who devote their lives to browsing through the pile and telling us what is worth our time and what isn't.
There are still some critics out there (Vulture, Pitchfork), but these sites are dying. They publish dozens of articles a day, trying to get as many clicks and pageviews as possible, adding to the volume of content we view daily. Before, you could reach for a magazine once a month or a watch a show once a week, but now you have to browse Vulture every day and read all 20+ articles they publish, even on the weekends. Who has time to read all that? Who has the time for any of this? Technology is making our lives harder, not easier.
So I guess the next question is, "How do I fix this?" Like mo

data.article_summary: 这篇文章展示了71种不同食物各自200卡路里的视觉对比。通过图片，读者可以直观地看到不同食物的卡路里密度差异。例如，200卡路里的芹菜重达1,425克，而同等卡路里的薯条仅73克。文章按卡路里密度从低到高排列，但没有讨论营养价值。所有图片使用相同尺寸的餐具拍摄，以保证对比的一致性。文章最后鼓励读者查看wiseGEEK网站以了解全部71种食物的比较。
data.comments_summary:

• neom认为很多人不了解卡路里的基本概念以及如何计算和控制卡路里摄入。他通过个人经历说明，即使像他妻子和母亲这样受过高等教育的人也对BMR（基础代谢率）和TDEE（总每日能量消耗）缺乏了解。他提出一个问题，是否很多人都对卡路里运作机制缺乏了解。

• sdwr对具体食物的卡路里密度表示怀疑，特别是对热狗和熟食火鸡的卡路里含量差异感到惊讶。他质疑热狗是否真的比熟食火鸡的卡路里密度高出三倍，并对食物的脂肪含量提出疑问。

• yellowapple的评论更侧重于对食物的直接反应，表达了对包含特定食物分量的餐食的兴趣，而没有深入讨论卡路里的问题。这显示出对实际饮食体验的关注，而不是对营养成分的技术性分析。

data.title: Someone got an LLM running on a Commodore 64 from 1982, and it runs as well
data.author: ghuntley
data.article_summary: "Llama2.c64" 是一个将 AI 模型移植到1982年发布的Commodore 64电脑上的项目，展示了在过时硬件上运行现代AI技术的可能性。该项目运行一个260K的“tinystories”模型，生成类似儿童讲述的故事，尽管性能不高，但在如此古老的硬件上实现AI运行令人印象深刻。项目创建者Maciej Witkowiak强调，该AI可在弱硬件上运行，并且生成结果的过程充满乐趣，尽管速度较慢。这个项目展示了在旧硬件上运行AI的潜力，也为AI模型在低功耗设备上的应用提供了启示。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于一个项目是否应被视为“大型语言模型”（Large Language Model, LLM）的定性讨论，以及对具体项目资源的分享。

不同观点：
• [oac] 认为该项目所使用的模型仅有260K参数，因此很难被视为一个“大型”语言模型。不过，他仍然认为这是一个很酷的项目。
• [JPLeRouzic] 提供了项目的代码库链接，并未直接参与是否为“大型”模型的讨论，而是通过分享资源来补充对话。

• [oac] 的观点聚焦于模型参数的数量，认为260K参数的模型不符合通常意义上“大型”语言模型的标准，这可能暗示“大型”通常与更大参数规模的模型相关联。
• [JPLeRouzic] 的回应则为对讨论的实际项目提供了进一步信息，帮助其他参与者获取项目资源以便深入了解或评估。

争议焦点：
• 主要争议在于模型规模的界定上，即260K参数的模型是否可以被视为“大型”语言模型。这一争议反映了不同参与者对“大型”的理解差异。

44023081.article_content:
Summary
Llama2.c64 is an attempt to get AI running on old hardware from 1982.
It runs a 260K tinystories model, bringing Llama2's capabilities to the Commodore 64.
Llama2.c64 creates child-like stories, showing impressive results for such outdated technology.
In the grand AI race, all sides are trying to get their LLMs working on the weakest, cheapest hardware possible. The weaker the hardware, the less power is required to run the LLMs. But how about getting an AI model running on hardware that came out in 1982?
That's exactly what Maciej Witkowiak is trying to do with their new project. Titled "Llama2.c64," this project aims to get a simple AI running on a Commodore 64, which came out long, long before LLMs were even a thing. And while it definitely won't be beating GPT-4o anytime soon, it's still an impressive feat.
Related
This mechanical keyboard will bring you back to the Commodore days
Yes, it comes with a joystick.
Posts
Llama2.c64 brings the new into the old, albeit slowly
As first reported by
Hackaday
, Maciej Witkowiak showed off Llama2.c64 to the world. As you might imagine, you're not going to get high performance out of this hardware, but getting anything running at all is really cool. Here's how Witkowiak describes it:
Ported to C64 by Maciej 'YTM/Elysium' Witkowiak using
oscar64
Llama2.c64 is a port of
llama2.c
to the Commodore C64 equipped with at least 2MB REU.
It runs the
260K tinystories model
bringing Llama2's capabilities to the unique C64 hardware environment.
This is not a chat model.
Rather, imagine prompting a 3-year-old child with the beginning of a story — they will continue it to the best of their vocabulary and abilities.
You can see an example of Llama2.c64 creating a story in the image above. Sure enough, it does sound like a child rambling on while telling a story, but given how little the AI was given to work with and how much it continued with the story, it's really amazing for a 42-year-old computer.
As part of the pros for this project, Witkowiak notes that the AI is under your control, works on weak hardware, and claims that "Waiting for the next token on a C64 is just as exciting as waiting for one coming from DeepSeek running on your laptop." Meanwhile, for the cons, there's "None really, this is fantastic" (albeit he admits it can be a little slow).
If you'd prefer to run an AI on something a little more powerful (but still weak enough to be impressive), check out these
eight SBCs perfect for running AI at home
. Also, you can read about that one time our writer, Ayush Pande,
turned his old PC into an AI image generation server
.

Stop building GPT wrappers. Build a world model instead.
Why Foundry exists:
Every SaaS app, enterprise tool, and internal workflow without an API will soon be automated by browser agents—not traditional API integrations. Tens of trillions of dollars in global labor depend on browser-based workflows that no AI system can reliably automate today.
But browser agents right now are like GPT-1: impressive demos, but brittle and broken in practice. To scale browser agents from GPT-1 demos to GPT-4 reliability—and unlock this enormous economic leap—they need purpose-built infrastructure:
Hyper-realistic, deterministic web simulations
Comprehensive annotation framework for labeling and debugging
Reliable benchmarks immune to web drift, IP bans, and rate limits
Robust RL training environments and infrastructure
No one's built it yet. We're going first.
We’re building exactly this—core infrastructure designed from first principles, specifically for browser agents. No incremental tools, no wrappers around GPT—just the foundational AI stack everyone else will depend on later.
Our founding team is ex-Scale AI & Meta
What we’re looking for:
A founding engineer who’s cracked at software engineering—but who now wants to ship core ML systems and RL infrastructure from scratch.
This is not another prompt-engineering job.

Build a browser agent gym—sparse rewards, non-determinism, messy DOM trees.

Are a killer engineer (Python, TypeScript)

Have real ML exposure: trained models, built infra, ran experiments.
Have strong OSS contributions, publications we’d recognize, or both.
Want a grind. Want to get better. Want to build something genuinely novel.
Bonus points:
You’ve built RL agents, browser automation (Puppeteer, Playwright), or eval tooling.
You’re tired of wrapping APIs and fine-tuning HuggingFace models—ready to do something deeper.

Real-world ML infrastructure, real users, real technical complexity.
Early equity, competitive pay, and massive growth trajectory.

If you’ve read this far, you probably get it.

Deterministic Web Simulation → Stable, reproducible testing with versioned web snapshots.

Automated Annotation & Labeling → Generate high-quality training data for benchmarking.

data.title: The Three C's of Meaningful Work
data.author: exiguus
data.article_summary:
文章讨论了如何通过三大要素——社区（Community）、贡献（Contribution）和挑战（Challenge）——让每一份工作都变得有意义。研究表明，有意义的工作能提升员工的参与度、工作满意度和留职率。领导者对员工的工作意义感有近50%的影响。

1. **社区**：通过开放的沟通和真实的联系建立归属感。例如，前美国公共卫生服务部长Vivek Murthy通过“内部 scoop”活动促进团队成员间的深度了解。
   
2. **贡献**：展示工作对他人产生的影响。Calendly的CEO通过分享客户如何利用节省的时间来体现员工工作的意义。

3. **挑战**：提供学习和成长的机会。McKinsey调查显示，缺乏职业发展是员工离职的主要原因。领导者通过挑战和支持员工的成长能提高参与度和留职率。

领导者在创造有意义的工作环境方面起着关键作用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：工作中的意义、管理方式以及员工的动机和满足感

不同观点：
• lowlystatsguy认为，尽管其工作具有高影响力且其团队成员能力强，但管理层的做法令人不满。他指出，管理层轻视单元测试的重要性，并且对开发流程缺乏深思熟虑，导致团队在紧急情况下不得不加班修复本可避免的错误。此外，管理层对新员工的态度以及对远程工作的回撤政策也引发了不满，认为公司利用“有意义的工作”作为压榨员工的借口。他认为，有意义的工作可以在任何地方找到，不应由公司定义。

• musicale则关注工作中的其他因素，如自主性、掌握感、目的性和新颖性。他认为，找到动机和工作意义之间存在联系，但并不完全相同。他指出，挑战与掌握感相关，而贡献感与目的性不同，自主性和新颖性也是重要的因素，但常被忽略。

补充讨论：
• lowlystatsguy通过具体事例（如单元测试的争议、管理层的言论、团队的不满调查结果）来支持其对管理层做法的批评，强调了员工在高要求工作环境下所承受的压力和不满。
• musicale提出了一种更为广泛的动机理论框架，认为除了挑战和贡献外，自主性和新颖性也是理解员工动机和满足感的重要维度。
• 争议的焦点在于如何平衡管理层的效率追求与员工的自主性和工作满足感。lowlystatsguy强调管理层的短视和员工的实际感受，而musicale则从更理论化的角度探讨了动机的多维性。

通过这两种观点的对比，可以看出，讨论的核心在于如何在实际工作中实现有意义的工作体验，同时满足管理效率和员工幸福感。

44022859.article_content:
Wes Adams and Tamara Myles
Meaningful Work
Career
The Three C’s of Meaningful Work
How every job can be meaningful with the guidance of a great leader.
Posted
May 18, 2025
|
Reviewed by Tyler Woods
Share
Tweet
Share on Bluesky
Share
Email
THE BASICS
What Is a Career
Take our Procrastination Test
Find a career counselor near me
Key points
Meaningful work comes from the three C's: community, contribution, and challenge.
Leaders account for nearly 50% of an individual employee's sense of meaning at work.
Moments of meaning can be found in every job, every day.
Meaning is the upstream factor that drives the outcomes we want as employees and organizational leaders.
In today’s rapidly evolving workplace, employees are seeking more than just a paycheck—they want meaning in their work. Research shows that meaningful work drives higher engagement, increased job satisfaction, and greater retention (Mercurio et al., 2023). But what exactly makes work meaningful, and how can leaders give their teams more of it?
Through years of studying high-performing organizations, we have identified three key factors that create meaning at work. These are the Three C’s—Community, Contribution, and Challenge (Adams & Myles, 2025). When these three elements are present, employees are not only more satisfied but also more motivated and productive.
1. Community: Fostering Authentic Connections
Humans are wired for connection, and the workplace is no exception. Studies show that employees who feel a strong sense of belonging are more engaged and productive (Ozcelik & Barsade, 2018). A Gallup study found that employees with a “best friend at work” are seven times more likely to be engaged than those without one (Rath & Harter, 2010).
Former U.S. Surgeon General Vivek Murthy, architect of the first Framework for Workplace Mental Health and Well-Being, shares a simple practice called the “Inside Scoop” that he uses on his own team to foster authentic connections (U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, 2022). At the start of each weekly team meeting, one person is asked to share a photo or object that is important to them and tell the story of why. During this brief interaction, that person is able to show a part of themselves that they value, and others on the call get a chance to know them more deeply. Murthy observed that this practice not only increased a sense of belonging, but also led to more
collaboration
among the team.
How to Build Community in Your Organization:
Encourage open and honest communication.
Foster authentic relationships through intentional connection.
Create shared experiences through team events and everyday storytelling.
2. Contribution: Showing the Impact of One’s Work
One of the strongest motivators in any job is the ability to see how one’s work benefits others. A study by Workhuman found that employees who find meaning in their work are 4.5 times more engaged
than those who don’t (Workhuman Analytics & Research Institute, 2019).
Tope Awotona, CEO of scheduling software company Calendly, makes a regular practice of showing people how their work matters. Calendly estimates that each person using their product saves an hour a week by avoiding the annoying back and forth of emailing to schedule meetings. Over the course of a year, that adds up to a full week of saved time. To bring that stat to life, Tope asks customers to share what they do with that extra hour. They might use it to do more meaningful work, or they may spend an extra hour with their families.
He then records a video for the whole organization to share the story of how Calendly impacted that customer. This helps to connect the dots between everyone’s daily work and the larger impact it has. That can be especially powerful for employees who aren’t customer facing, such as software engineers who spend most of their time coding alone.

3. **挑战**：提供学习和成长的机会。McKinsey调查显示，缺乏职业发展是员工离职的主要原因。领导者通过挑战和支持员工的成长能提高参与度和留职率。

data.article_summary: 《开放问题项目》由Erik D. Demaine、Joseph S. B. Mitchell和Joseph O’Rourke编辑，旨在记录计算几何及相关领域的重要未解问题。项目始于2001年，最初公布了30个问题，现已增至75个以上。虽然不再接受新问题提交，但鼓励对现有问题进行更新，特别是已部分或完全解决的问题。更新可通过Github Pull Request进行。每个问题都有唯一编号和分类，问题列表可按类别或编号浏览，涵盖排列、艺术画廊、着色、组合几何、数据结构、凸包、几何图、图绘制等多个主题。项目还提供了所有问题的PDF文件以供查阅。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：开放性数学与计算机科学问题的收集和管理，以及技术（尤其是人工智能技术）在解决问题中的潜在应用。

不同观点：
• jll29：支持建立一个系统化的开放问题数据库，包含问题名称、编号、状态更新和相关文献参考。认为这种做法应推广到数学和计算机科学的各个子领域，并提到数学家Terence Tao等正在探索通过技术支持的远程合作方式解决问题。建议将问题清单、证明收集、现有数据集（如OEIS）以及Jupyter笔记本等工具整合到一起，形成完整的体系。

• wrsh07：关注当前讨论中的具体问题是否仍然有效和有意义，提到了O'Rourke、Demaine和Mitchell等人在离散和计算几何领域的贡献，并引用了具体的书籍和研究成果（如MoMA的折纸收藏和PTAS算法）。其讨论更偏向于确认信息的时效性和实用性。

• mazsa：关注是否有类似https://www.cs.ru.nl/~freek/100/ 上的解决方案，即寻找现有的、已经整理好的问题解决方案，显示出对实际问题解决进展的兴趣。

• lordfrito：对文章中缺乏视觉元素（如图片）表示失望，个人兴趣偏向于更具视觉吸引力的内容，而非纯文本或技术性讨论。

• ogogmad：提出新的机器学习技术（尤其是AI）在解决开放问题中的潜力，提到DeepMind发现的新的最小曲面不变量，并设想AI是否能发明出如同调群一样强大的数学概念。认为AI可以通过构建具有预测能力的压缩器来帮助解决几何问题，显示出对AI技术前景的乐观态度。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：目前讨论中并未出现直接的争议，但不同参与者关注点明显不同。例如，lordfrito对文章的呈现形式有不同期望，而ogogmad则对AI的潜力持积极态度，其他参与者则更关注问题的具体管理和技术支持。

• 重要论据：jll29和wrsh07都引用了具体的学术资源和实践案例（如OEIS、MoMA收藏等），以支持其观点。ogogmad则引用了DeepMind在AI领域的具体成果，以证明AI在数学问题解决中的潜力。

• 讨论关系：mazsa的问题引导了关于现有解决方案的讨论，而ogogmad的评论则进一步扩展到AI技术的潜在应用，显示出讨论从具体问题向技术前景的自然延伸。

data.title: Living beings emit a faint light that extinguishes upon death
data.author: geox
data.article_summary: 一项新研究发现，所有生物体都会自发地发射一种极微弱的生物光（超弱光子发射，UPE），这种光在死亡后消失。研究人员通过使用高敏感度的摄像设备比较活体和死亡小鼠的UPE，发现活体小鼠的UPE强度显著高于刚死亡的小鼠。在植物中，UPE强度受温度、损伤和化学处理等压力因素的影响而变化，受伤部位的UPE比未受伤部位更亮。UPE与细胞代谢产生的活性氧（ROS）有关，ROS在应激反应中起信号作用，但过度产生会导致氧化应激，从而引发UPE。这项研究表明，UPE可以作为动物生命力和植物应激反应的敏感指标，并可能应用于非侵入性的诊断和医学研究工具。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Kirlian摄影的有效性和意义

不同观点：
• 观点一：对Kirlian摄影持怀疑态度。有用户认为Kirlian摄影只是一种视觉现象，并没有实际的科学依据或超自然意义。例子：有些人指出，Kirlian摄影只是捕捉到了物体在高压电场下的电晕放电现象，并不能反映任何神秘的能量场或气场。

• 观点二：支持Kirlian摄影具有超自然或能量场的捕捉能力。有用户相信Kirlian摄影可以拍摄到人或物体的气场或能量场，认为它揭示了肉眼看不见的维度。例子：有用户提到，Kirlian摄影能够显示出人在不同情绪状态下的能量场变化。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：Kirlian摄影的科学性与超自然性之间的争议。怀疑者强调其物理原理，支持者则侧重其可能的超自然解释。
• 其他值得注意的讨论点：Kirlian摄影在艺术和心理学等领域的应用，有人认为它可以作为一种工具来探索人类情感和能量状态。

Living beings emit a faint light that extinguishes upon death, according to a new study
by
Sanjukta Mondal
, Phys.org
Credit:
The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
(2025). DOI: 10.1021/acs.jpclett.4c03546
The light of someone's life might not be just another person, but light in the literal sense. According to a recent study by researchers from University of Calgary, every living system emits light without requiring external excitation due to a biological phenomenon known as ultraweak photon emission (UPE).
In
mice
, UPE was linked to vitality as live mice emitted significantly higher UPE intensity compared to recently dead mice. In plants, however, UPE varied depending on exposure to stress factors like temperature changes, injury and chemical treatments, as
reported
in
The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
.
Living organisms are compact biochemical labs where complex chemical reactions keep the system up and running. Cellular metabolism, a series of chemical reactions that fuel life-sustaining processes, produces a group of highly reactive oxygen-containing molecules produced as a natural byproduct called
reactive oxygen species
or ROS.
Studies suggest that ROS plays a central role in UPE. When organisms encounter stress, they activate biochemical pathways that generate ROS, which act as signaling molecules in the
cellular stress response
. However, excessive ROS production can lead to
oxidative stress
, overwhelming the cell's antioxidant defenses. This oxidative stress can induce electron excitation and transfer processes, ultimately resulting in UPE.
High-sensitivity EMCCD and CCD cameras for imaging UPE in dark, controlled environments. Credit:
The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
(2025). DOI: 10.1021/acs.jpclett.4c03546
Unlike bioluminescence, which produces high-intensity light visible to the naked eye, UPE, also known as biophoton emission, is a spontaneous release of extremely low-intensity light that is invisible to the human eye and falls within the spectral range of 200–1,000 nm. This faint light has been detected in a wide range of life forms—from
single-celled organisms
and bacteria to plants, animals, and even humans.
Despite being so widely observed, not much is known about the impact of mortality and stress factors on UPE. Furthermore, the ability to monitor UPE in response to stress factors and injuries could be a powerful, non-invasive tool for diagnostics and medical research.
The researchers used advanced imaging techniques to explore the biological significance of UPE by directly comparing emissions in living versus dead animals, while also systematically visualizing the effects of temperature, injury, and chemical treatments on UPE in plants.
Effect of the temperature on the intensity of UPE in plants. Credit:
The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
(2025). DOI: 10.1021/acs.jpclett.4c03546
To carry out the experiments, the researchers designed ultradark enclosures to eliminate environmental light interference. They then used an Electron-Multiplying Charge-Coupled Device (EMCCD) camera for imaging plants and a Charge-Coupled Device (CCD) camera with IVIS system to image UPE changes in mice.
The results revealed that despite both groups having the same body temperature of 37°C, the live mice showed robust emissions, whereas the UPE from the euthanized mice was nearly extinguished. In plants, an increase in temperature and injuries led to an increase in UPE intensity. Injured sites were consistently brighter than uninjured parts—a change in the former was observed once the site received any chemical treatment.
This study establishes that UPE can act as a sensitive indicator of vitality in animals and of stress responses in plants. The researchers suggest that these findings could catalyze the application of UPE imaging as a non-invasive technique for both basic biological research and clinical diagnostics.
More information:
V. Salari et al, Imaging Ultraweak Photon Emission from Living and Dead Mice and from Plants under Stress,
The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
(2025).

44022272.article_summary: 一项新研究发现，所有生物体都会自发地发射一种极微弱的生物光（超弱光子发射，UPE），这种光在死亡后消失。研究人员通过使用高敏感度的摄像设备比较活体和死亡小鼠的UPE，发现活体小鼠的UPE强度显著高于刚死亡的小鼠。在植物中，UPE强度受温度、损伤和化学处理等压力因素的影响而变化，受伤部位的UPE比未受伤部位更亮。UPE与细胞代谢产生的活性氧（ROS）有关，ROS在应激反应中起信号作用，但过度产生会导致氧化应激，从而引发UPE。这项研究表明，UPE可以作为动物生命力和植物应激反应的敏感指标，并可能应用于非侵入性的诊断和医学研究工具。

data.title: France Becomes First Government to Endorse UN Open Source Principles
data.author: bzg
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：法国政府及开放源代码（Open Source）政策的可信度及其实际执行情况，以及全球对开放源代码软件的采用和影响。

不同观点：
• **对法国政府开放源代码承诺的怀疑**：[idoubtit] 认为法国政府虽然宣称支持开放源代码，但实际资金仍流向专有软件，例如与微软签订的大合同。这种行为与政府宣称的政策相悖。
• **支持开放源代码作为建立信任的手段**：[fdefitte] 认为政府软件应默认开源，这将有助于建立公众信任，并可能在长远上区分民主与专制政体。
• **比较不同国家的开源政策**：[somat] 提到美国的开源原则，软件默认进入公共领域，并提供了相关链接。
• **全球向开源软件迁移的愿景**：[rr808] 希望全球能够从Windows/MacOS/iOS/Android等专有系统转向开源软件，以减少对美国科技公司的依赖。
• **法国政府在开放源代码方面的积极实践**：[patcon] 指出自2017年以来，法国政府在开放源代码方面的前瞻性思考和实践，例如与ETAlab的互动。

补充讨论：
• **政策执行力与实际效果的质疑**：[canvascritic] 认为关键在于法国政府是否会真正调整采购渠道和供应商要求，否则这只是一个宣言。
• **对LLM（大型语言模型）和开源定义的讨论**：[andy99] 关注开源政策是否涵盖LLM，以及如何定义开源，特别是希望看到对Meta等公司“开放”策略的拒绝。
• **开放源代码的文化象征与现实**：[pmarreck] 通过电影《Tron: Legacy》中的情节，表达了对企业贪婪的抗议和开放源代码的文化象征意义。
• **开放源代码与公共设施的关系**：[twodave] 作为美国人，讨论了在资本主义社会中哪些应构成公共设施，并质疑美国是否能接受类似法国的开源政策。
• **开放源代码政策中的许可证问题**：[ksec] 质疑开放源代码的定义，特别是是否仅限于GPL或AGPL。
• **联合国在开放源代码解决方案中的角色**：[nashashmi] 提问联合国能在开放源代码解决方案中扮演什么角色。
• **对联合国推动全球开源采用的关注**：[MilnerRoute] 希望看到更多关于联合国推动开放源代码采用的报道，并提供了相关链接。

争议的焦点：法国政府是否真正落实开放源代码政策，以及全球其他国家（特别是美国）是否能接受并实施类似的开源政策。此外，开放源代码的定义和许可证问题也是讨论中的一个重要争议点。

data.author: cenazoic
data.article_summary: 《虚构研究期刊》每年11月出版一期虚构的学术研究摘要，这些作品由真实的学术人员创作，旨在通过创意写作帮助研究人员摆脱日常研究的束缚，享受写作的乐趣。期刊由Kay Guccione博士和Matthew Cheeseman博士编辑，最初通过创意写作工作坊发展而来，帮助研究人员以富有想象力的方式传达他们的研究。该期刊的所有卷期均可免费下载。2024年的主题是“繁荣”，鼓励作者想象一个因研究而繁荣的未来，作品可以是讽刺、评论或戏剧性的，且无需对主题做具体解释。期刊出版虚构研究摘要旨在鼓励享受写作的过程，重塑与写作的积极关系。

44003928.article_content:
The Journal of Imaginary Research publishes short works of fiction in the academic genre of the Research Abstract.
Find and download all of our volumes to date here
.
The imagined research abstracts, and their imagined researchers were constructed by real academic staff, research staff, and research students. We, Dr Kay Guccione (
connect on LinkedIn here
) and Dr Matthew Cheeseman, produce a new Volume of the Journal of Imaginary Research each November, as November is Global Academic Writing Month.
In the early phases we used a workshop of imaginative writing practices (
download the workshop materials here
) to support writers to construct and refine fictional abstracts and biographies that are freed from the confines of day-to-day research projects. Each piece is rooted in a real image, carried into the workshop by a real researcher.
In developing this workshop we wanted to introduce creative writing concepts to researchers working in any and all disciplines, as a way to support people who felt tense, anxious, about writing, or had fallen into a negative relationship with their writing.
The pieces in
these volumes
were by-products of our workshop, helping researchers reflect on how they can creatively communicate their own research projects, and how they can find the joy of creativity within the grind of productivity. Creativity is a property of all writers and the privilege of all researchers.
We now accept submissions each November from any writer who sees the value of using creative processes, and writing for fun. Our next call will be announced on this blog site, when we are ready to receive new submissions.
Below, Kay presents a paper on the origin story and pedagogical underpinnings of the Journal at the
Creative Experiment in the Classroom Conference
, GCU London, June 2020.
Dr Kay Guccione (
@kayguccione
) Head of Researcher Development, and Dr Matthew Cheeseman (
@eine
) Associate Professor in Creative Writing
— Editors.
Volume 10
Download
The Journal of Imaginary Research is now accepting submissions of new short
fictional
pieces for our annual volume produced each November to celebrate Global Academic Writing Month. We publish
imaginary
research abstracts, and
all our volumes are available as free downloads
.
Deadline
5pm on Friday 6
th
December, 2024
What do we mean
imaginary
research abstracts?
We mean short works of fiction, that take a format that is familiar to us as researchers and academics. An abstract is the summary of an academic paper, that gives us a succinct overview of the research that has been done, and the new outcomes or ideas that the research has generated.
The 2024 theme
: Flourishing
For this year’s theme we’ve been inspired by
Ayana Elizabeth Johnson’s book on radical imagination
that asks ‘What if we get it right?… What if we act as if we love the future?’ We ask, what if we
flourish
?
Well, what if our research projects and agendas get it right? What if we
flourish
? What if our research creates positive momentum? What if because of our work, more people are thriving? What might this mean for our work and for the disciplines that we work in? What might this mean for the support we receive from funders, the media and even our family and friends? We’re not suggesting that you cure cancer or end war, but we are asking you to imagine a future that is flourishing as a result of research. What would take us there, What work is still left to be done? What are the next steps we will take from this imaginary space of flourishing? Perhaps there have been great costs in achieving such a future, perhaps new problems have presented themselves, or perhaps—even—it’s more of the same.
We’d like you to interpret the theme in your own way so that your submission relates to
flourishing
in some way. You don’t need to explain this to us or within your piece. It’s fine to take the theme literally, and write with a flourish. It’s also fine to use the theme as a way to kick start your imagination. Where will your imaginary research go to?
Remember too, that the biography of the imaginary researcher that accompanies your fictional abstract is a good way of introducing satire, commentary and drama into your work. What sort of researcher might produce the imaginary research you are concocting? Is there a counterpoint in their biography, or something that affirms the work they are doing? How can you use the biography to enhance the fictional aspect of your work. This is your opportunity to indulge in both characterisation and worldbuilding.
Keep reading to find out how to get started and how to submit your writing…
Why do we publish fictional research?
We publish imagined research abstracts as works of fiction firstly because writing for enjoyment is a good thing to encourage. We spend a lot of time trying to reduce our anxiety about writing, and so writing imaginatively is a good way to reshape our relationship with writing into something creative and enjoyable.

主要讨论点：便携式低能量高分辨率X射线系统的应用及其潜在市场

不同观点：
• burnt-resistor认为，在多种行业中，尤其是无损检测（NDT）焊缝检查以及普通零件的可用性检查中，需要更多的低能量、高分辨率的便携式X射线系统，以发现隐藏的疲劳和裂纹。此外，他还提到这一技术可能对铁匠检查定制物品的强度和质量有帮助，甚至可能进入家庭医疗领域，用于家庭医疗X射线系统。

补充讨论：
• burnt-resistor指出，美国临床环境中存在高能量CT扫描的过度使用问题，暗示低能量X射线系统可能是一个更合适、更可持续的选择，特别是在不需要高能量扫描的情况下。这可能意味着对现有技术的反思和改进方向。

• 论据中提到了多个应用场景，包括工业无损检测、定制金属制品的质量评估以及潜在的医疗应用，显示出这种技术具有广泛的市场潜力。

• 争议焦点可能在于低能量X射线系统是否能够在临床和工业应用中取代或补充现有的高能量技术，特别是在诊断准确性和安全性方面的比较。

• burnt-resistor认为，在多种行业中，尤其是无损检测（NDT）焊缝检查以及普通零件的可用性检查中，需要更多的低能量、高分辨率的便携式X射线系统，以发现隐藏的疲劳和裂纹。此外，他还提到这一技术可能对铁匠检查定制物品的强度和质量有帮助，甚至可能进入家庭医疗领域，用于家庭医疗X射线系统。

补充讨论：
• burnt-resistor指出，美国临床环境中存在高能量CT扫描的过度使用问题，暗示低能量X射线系统可能是一个更合适、更可持续的选择，特别是在不需要高能量扫描的情况下。这可能意味着对现有技术的反思和改进方向。

• 论据中提到了多个应用场景，包括工业无损检测、定制金属制品的质量评估以及潜在的医疗应用，显示出这种技术具有广泛的市场潜力。

• 争议焦点可能在于低能量X射线系统是否能够在临床和工业应用中取代或补充现有的高能量技术，特别是在诊断准确性和安全性方面的比较。

data.title: A New Headache for Honest Students: Proving They Didn't Use A.I
data.author: ripe
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：学生在学习中依赖AI工具的现状及其影响

不同观点：
• Glyptodon的观点：他的一位计算机科学（CS）专业的朋友抱怨同学们过度依赖AI写代码，导致他们在组项目中无法贡献有效代码，且自己因手工写代码时忽略一些小错误（如分号）而被扣分，感到沮丧。他还担心这可能会影响未来就业。
   
• kayodelycaon的观点：提到一位教授因学生使用AI写论文而几乎让全班不及格，很多学生没有检查AI生成的内容，甚至出现如“like and subscribe”这样的网络用语。此外，学生在考试中的书写和语法能力也令人担忧，教授面临来自校方的压力要求让学生通过。

• spondylosaurus的观点：对学生需要证明自己作业的“人性化”感到惊讶，特别是计算机科学的教授应该了解这些AI“检测”工具的不可靠性。

• jasonthorsness的观点：他的孩子在中学和高中就读，他认为目前教育系统正在实时应对AI带来的挑战。他预计未来会更多依赖于个人信任、纸质考试和手写作业，并认为这种回归传统的方式可能反而是最好的解决方案。

• mbil的观点：提出未来可能会有程序生成模拟人类打字习惯的论文，暗示这将是一场技术军备竞赛。

• gxs的观点：对写作论文的传统要求持批评态度，认为要求固定页数的论文很 arbitrary（武断），并希望未来的评估更注重答案的质量而非数量。

• ta112321的观点：作为助教（TA），他发现作弊现象显著增加，尤其是使用低级手段作弊的学生。尽管AI使用检测工具不完善，但现有工具主要用于检测直接复制粘贴的行为。他还提到作弊行为猖獗可能与COVID期间的教育中断有关，并建议在招聘时对“COVID一代”持谨慎态度，增加类似MCAT/GRE/LSAT的监考方式。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于AI在教育中的使用和滥用问题。一方面，学生依赖AI导致基础技能（如写代码、写作能力）的下降；另一方面，教育机构在评估和防止作弊方面面临挑战，教授和学生都感到压力。
• 讨论还涉及到未来教育评估方式的可能变化，包括回归纸笔考试和增加监考等措施，以应对AI带来的作弊风险。
• 对AI检测工具的可靠性存在质疑，特别是在判断学生作业是否由AI生成时，存在误判的可能性。

data.title: KDE is finally getting a native virtual machine manager called "Karton"
data.author: bundie
data.article_summary: KDE Plasma将迎来一款全新的虚拟机管理器——Karton，旨在为KDE用户提供更契合桌面环境的虚拟化工具。目前，Karton由滑铁卢大学学生Derek Lin通过2025年Google Summer of Code项目开发，使用Qt Quick和Kirigami构建，并通过libvirt API管理虚拟机。Karton的目标包括通过libvirt的XML格式安装和配置虚拟机、实现自定义SPICE查看器、支持快照功能、以及更精细的虚拟机控制和直观的用户界面。开发还关注减少延迟、支持多种操作系统和图形处理器使用情况的展示，并计划兼容移动设备。该项目预计于2025年6月开始编码，目标在同年9月前完成。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：新推出的基于Qt的virt-manager替代工具的优缺点及使用体验

不同观点：
• [fishgoesblub] 认为新的替代工具虽然不错，但使用Kirigami和Qt Quick开发让他感到失望。他指出，相比Qt Widgets，Kirigami和Qt Quick在界面外观和功能上表现较差。
• [hagbard_c] 对工具的名称进行了调侃，指出"Karton"在荷兰语中意为"纸板"，并猜测该名称可能与工具用于处理虚拟机（虚拟盒子）有关。
• [shmerl] 对新工具表示欢迎，并提到自己长期使用virt-manager，对更符合KDE生态的解决方案表示支持。同时，他期待virt-manager能通过libvirt添加对Vulkan渲染的支持。此外，他提到使用Kirigami的界面往往有过多的边距，导致视觉上不太紧凑，例如print-manager的配置界面。

补充讨论：
• 关于Kirigami和Qt Quick的争议：[fishgoesblub] 和 [shmerl] 都提到Kirigami的界面设计问题，尤其是边距和视觉感受，反映出部分用户对Kirigami和Qt Quick在实际使用中的不满。
• 对virt-manager功能扩展的期待：[shmerl] 提到对Vulkan渲染支持的期待，显示出用户对virt-manager及其替代工具功能扩展的需求和关注。
• 名称的幽默解读：[hagbard_c] 的评论虽然幽默，但也引发了对工具名称选择的联想和讨论。

争议焦点：Kirigami和Qt Quick在界面设计上的优劣，以及是否适合用于此类工具的开发。用户[fishgoesblub] 和 [shmerl] 对此有明显的负面评价，而[shmerl] 还指出了具体的问题，如边距过多。

44024784.article_content:
If you spend most of your time in GNOME, you've probably used something like GNOME Boxes to spin up virtual machines without much hassle. We actually gave it a shoutout in our
list of essential Linux apps for newcomers
this year. KDE users, however, have often found themselves relying on
tools such as virt-manager
or
even GNOME Boxes itself
. While functional, these don't always feel perfectly at home within the Plasma desktop, and the old
qt-virt-manager
, a Qt-based alternative, has seen its development stall for years.
Now, a new Virtual Machine Manager is
in the works for KDE Plasma
. The project, named Karton, has roots dating back to Aaron Rainbolt's original effort to build a QEMU frontend using its command line interface. Later, KDE developer Harald Sitter took over and developed it as a Google Summer of Code project.
Currently, Karton is
actively developed
by Derek Lin, a University of Waterloo student participating in Google Summer of Code 2025. His primary aim is to deliver a virtual machine manager that truly belongs in the KDE ecosystem.
To feel right at home in KDE, Karton is being built with Qt Quick and Kirigami. It uses the libvirt API to handle virtual machines and could eventually work across different platforms.
Right now, development is focused on getting the core parts in place. Lin is working on a new domain installer that ditches direct
virt-install
calls in favor of libosinfo, which helps detect OS images and generate the right libvirt XML for setting up virtual machines more precisely. He's still refining device configuration and working on broader hypervisor support. Another key part of the work is building a custom SPICE viewer using Qt Quick from scratch:
If you're curious, here's the list of specific deliverables Lin i
ncluded in his GSoC proposal
, though he notes the proposal itself is a bit outdated:
Install and configure virtual machines through libvirt’s XML format instead of virt-install CLI
Add ability to configure commonly used options in UI
Allows for more fine-tuned control of virtual machine options
Implement a custom
SPICE
viewer to allow users to interact with and view the active virtual machine (instead of virt-viewer
Virtual machine snapshots to restore/backup previous states
Intuitive UI for displaying virtual machines
Making a user-friendly and aesthetically pleasing GUI by addressing community feedback
Referencing
MacOS UTM list layout
and a preview of the VM
Making UI convergent (mobile-friendly)
Retrieving virtual machine status updates using the libvirt API virEventRegisterImpl function instead of using the default built-in event loop.
Allows it to be integrated with custom Qt event loops
Reduces current latency with loading virtual machine list page
Adding a browse tool which lists commonly installed operating systems
GPU/memory usage graph as done in virt-manager
Feature to switch between connecting to
QEMU hypervisor with session (user) and system (root)
.
GNOME Boxes seems to only support “session”, however adding support for “system” could be useful for non-KVM/Linux backends like bhyve (FreeBSD) or Hyper-V
For those interested in the timeline, Lin's GSoC proposal says the official GSoC coding starts June 2, 2025. The goal is to have a working app ready by the midterm evaluation around July 14, 2025, with the final submission due September 1, 2025.

data.title: California vanity license plate applications with reasons for rejection
data.author: networked
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了加州车管局（DMV）收到的个性化车牌申请数据。数据来自一个包含23,463条申请的CSV文件，时间范围为2015-2016年，仅包括被审查委员会标记需要额外审查的申请。文件包含车牌组合、审查原因代码、申请人解释的意义、审查员评论和状态（批准或拒绝）等信息。数据源自458个Excel工作簿，部分记录缺失信息，且可能存在结构不一致导致的错误。审查标准包括避免淫秽、冒犯、误导或贬低特定群体的词汇。数据中含有一些不雅语言，审查原因代码详细规定了拒绝车牌的各类情况。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：加州DMV定制车牌的审批过程、 rejections的原因及其合理性

不同观点：
• OptionOfT认为，加州DMV没有集中存储数据，否则不会出现多种格式。同时提到DMV的流程较为落后，仍然依赖纸质和手工处理。
• MrFoof分享了自己因缩写问题被拒绝的经历，并对审批过程的效率表示不满。
• chmod775对DMV能够解读出一个具有威胁性含义的车牌表示惊讶，认为审查人员很厉害。
• Gigachad认为一些拒绝理由过于敏感，特别是对“gaymer”和“air$oft”这样的词的拒绝没有合理依据，指出许多拒绝是基于性别玩笑或种族主义。
• starkparker提到一个在Oregon州列出定制车牌的机器人，并将讨论引向不同州的政策差异。
• runlevel1提供了Google Sheet版本的数据，并指出对数据进行了规范化处理，包括翻译和重新排序。
• savrajsingh分享了一个因文化背景不同而导致拒绝的例子，指出“13”在加州被视为帮派参考，并提出关于言论自由的讨论。
• davchana指出加州DMV的最新申请表不再要求解释车牌含义。
• burnt-resistor对“REDROCK”被拒绝表示不解，指出同名咖啡店存在。
• no_wizard以幽默方式表达了对“ASSMAN”无法通过审批的遗憾。
• josephcsible列举了一系列被拒绝的例子，认为许多拒绝理由不合理，批评官僚主义的过度干预。
• netsharc提到一个俄语短语被拒绝的例子，并提供了该短语的翻译链接。
• silisili对“DAVES88”因与希特勒相关的理由被拒绝表示不满，认为大多数人不会联想到此含义。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于DMV对车牌审批的拒绝理由是否合理。一些用户认为某些拒绝过于敏感或不必要，而另一些用户则对DMV能够识别潜在威胁表示赞赏。
• 讨论中还涉及了不同州的车牌政策差异，以及加州DMV在数据管理和审批流程上的落后问题。
• 一些用户对特定文化背景或语言问题导致的拒绝表示不解，并提出言论自由的论点。

California license plates
Warning: this dataset contains vulgar and offensive language (quite a lot of it).
applications.csv
is a CSV of 23,463 personalized license plate applications the California DMV received from 2015-2016.
These do NOT represent all applications received by the DMV during that timeframe, only applications that were flagged for additional review by the Review Committee. The file includes the following columns:
plate
: the personalized license plate combination requested.
review_reason_code
: Reason code for the application being reviewed (see below for codes).
customer_meaning
: Meaning of the plate provided by the applicant.
reviewer_comments
: Comments from DMV reviewers.
status
:
Y
means the plate was approved,
N
means it was denied.
This data was parsed from a set of 458 Excel workbooks that the DMV prepared for someone else's public records request. I received the files as a consolation prize in response to my own related records request, which I was told would cost $2,000 to fulfill otherwise.
Notes
In plate combinations, a
#
character indicates a hand symbol, a
$
character indicates the heart symbol, a
+
character indicates the plus symbol, and a
&
character indicates the star symbol.
Some records are missing reason codes, customer meanings, reviewer comments, and/or statuses.
A reviewer comment of "No micro" indicates that a paper application was submitted but was unavailable in the DMV's imaging system.
In a few cases the reason code is some other character or word besides
Y
or
N
, possibly a typo.
I tried to redact any records I found that seemed to include too much personal information about the applicant (about 50 in total).
Because the data is parsed from Excel workbooks that are not 100% consistent in structure, there may be some errors.
Review reason codes are described as follows:
7(B) When a desired configuration is not available, a letter shall not be substituted for a number, nor shall a number be substituted for a letter, to create another configuration of a similar appearance.
7(D) The department shall refuse any configuration that may carry connotations offensive to good taste and decency, or which would be misleading, based on criteria which includes, but is not limited to, the following:
1. The configuration has a sexual connotation or is a term of lust or depravity.
2. The configuration is a vulgar term; a term of contempt, prejudice, or hostility; an insulting or degrading term; a racially degrading term; or an ethnically degrading term.
3. The configuration is a swear word or term considered profane, obscene, or repulsive.
4. The configuration has a negative connotation to a specific group.
5. The configuration misrepresents a law enforcement entity.
6. The configuration has been deleted from regular series license plates.
7. The configuration is a foreign or slang word or term, or is a phonetic spelling or mirror image of a word or term falling into the categories described in subdivisions 1. through 6. above.

44025022.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了加州车管局（DMV）收到的个性化车牌申请数据。数据来自一个包含23,463条申请的CSV文件，时间范围为2015-2016年，仅包括被审查委员会标记需要额外审查的申请。文件包含车牌组合、审查原因代码、申请人解释的意义、审查员评论和状态（批准或拒绝）等信息。数据源自458个Excel工作簿，部分记录缺失信息，且可能存在结构不一致导致的错误。审查标准包括避免淫秽、冒犯、误导或贬低特定群体的词汇。数据中含有一些不雅语言，审查原因代码详细规定了拒绝车牌的各类情况。

• 讨论中还涉及了不同州的车牌政策差异，以及加州DMV在数据管理和审批流程上的落后问题。

主要讨论点：围绕Coinbase用户信息泄露事件的隐私与安全问题，以及对加密货币带来的风险和个人防护措施的讨论。

不同观点：
• **neilv** 强调了事件的严重性，指出多达97,000名客户的个人信息被盗，包括加密货币余额和实际地址。他重述了事件，突出了信息泄露对用户造成的潜在风险。

• **TheKidCoder** 持相对淡定的态度，认为这种情况并非加密货币独有，而是所有财富形式都可能遭遇的问题。他指出，犯罪分子为了获取财富会不择手段，因此问题本质上与财富的吸引力有关，而非仅仅加密货币的问题。

• **lsllc** 引用了xkcd漫画来表达对信息泄露事件的担忧，并通过两个不同的漫画链接暗示了加密货币和隐私问题在更广泛背景下的预见性。他特别提到对其中一个漫画（#2203）中的场景更为担忧，暗示了对未来潜在风险的警惕。

• **OutOfHere** 提供了具体的个人防护建议，主张用户不应炫耀自己的加密货币资产，并避免在手机上显示与加密货币相关的应用程序或小部件。此外，他还指出，持有传统ETF（如IBIT）相对更加安全，暗示加密货币带来的额外风险。

补充讨论：
• 评论之间存在一定的回应关系。**neilv** 和 **TheKidCoder** 的观点形成了对比，**neilv** 强调了事件的直接影响，而 **TheKidCoder** 则试图淡化事件的特殊性，将其与更广泛的犯罪动机联系起来。
• **lsllc** 的评论则通过引用漫画引入了一种幽默但警示性的视角，指出了对加密货币相关风险的预见性。
• **OutOfHere** 的评论则提供了实际的防护建议，强调个人在面对此类风险时可以采取的具体措施。

争议焦点：评论中并没有直接的冲突，但不同评论者对事件的严重性和应对措施的看法存在差异。一些人认为这是加密货币特有的风险（如 **neilv**），而另一些人则认为这是所有财富形式都面临的问题（如 **TheKidCoder**）。此外，**OutOfHere** 强调了传统金融工具的相对安全性，暗示了对加密货币风险的担忧。

data.author: austinallegro

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：针对《经济学人》杂志的定价策略及其在不同国家和地区之间的差异，评论者表达了不同的看法和经验。

不同观点：
• [jonahhorowitz] 认为《当前事务》杂志上的一篇文章对《经济学人》的分析非常出色，暗示该文章对理解《经济学人》的定位和市场策略有帮助。

• [comrade1234] 指出，尽管印度和巴基斯坦整体经济水平较低，但中上阶层拥有相对较高的财富。这些富裕人群有能力支付比其他人更高的订阅费用，甚至超过像美国湾区技术行业管理人员这样的人。他还提到，他的一些朋友在这些国家享有高生活水平，比如拥有私人司机、住家厨师和育儿保姆，因此他们可以负担更高的订阅费用。

• [slyall] 分享了自己的经历，指出《经济学人》的定价策略在过去较为统一，但后来逐渐根据不同国家的市场情况进行了调整。他提到自己曾通过更改地址来获取较低的价格，并提供了自己十年前关于定价的博客文章作为参考。

• [tracerbulletx] 则从商业角度解释了这种定价策略，认为公司根据不同市场的消费者行为和价格/销量动态调整价格是基本的商业操作，属于“商业101”的常识。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于《经济学人》的定价策略是否合理。部分评论者如[comrade1234]通过个人经验说明不同地区富裕人群的支付能力，而[slyall]则通过实际操作展示了如何应对定价差异。

• [tracerbulletx] 的观点则强调了这种定价策略在商业上的合理性，认为这是市场细分和利润最大化的常见手段。

• 评论之间还隐含了对全球经济不平等的讨论，尤其是[comrade1234]提到的印度和巴基斯坦的中上阶层与普通消费者之间的财富差距。

data.title: The effect of physical fitness on mortality is overestimated
data.author: gnabgib
data.article_summary: 一项新研究表明，体能对降低过早死亡风险的作用可能被高估。乌普萨拉大学的研究人员分析了1972年至1995年间110万名瑞典男性的征兵数据，根据他们18岁时的体能水平，追踪其至60岁或直到去世。尽管高体能水平与较低的心血管疾病和癌症死亡风险相关，但研究发现，高体能男性在随机事故（如车祸、溺水和凶杀）中的死亡风险也较低，这与预期不符。这表明，高体能和低体能群体在其他重要方面可能存在差异，以前的研究未充分考虑这些因素，导致效果被高估。研究使用了负对照结果分析和兄弟比较设计来验证结果。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：运动健身与意外死亡风险之间的关系，以及健身对整体寿命和生活质量的影响。

不同观点：
• Noumenon72认为，死于随机意外（如车祸、凶杀）的人与其他人不同，他们往往受教育程度较低、做决策较差、生活环境更危险，甚至与移民背景有关。他批评科学界对“所有事情都是相关的”这一事实反应迟缓。
• yakbarber不同意研究中“健身与随机意外死亡无关”的假设，提出健身的人可能有更好的反应能力、协调性和恢复能力，从而降低死亡风险。
• gdudeman指出，职业锻炼和休闲锻炼的效果可能不同，休闲锻炼的人通常属于不同的社会经济群体，这可能是导致健康差异的原因。
• andrewl更关注健康寿命而非单纯的长寿，认为健身特别是良好的肌肉质量对维持自主生活能力很重要。
• amazingamazing对高强度锻炼的价值持怀疑态度，认为从久坐生活方式转变为适度锻炼有很大价值，但从适度到高强度锻炼的收益则不确定。
• akamaka认为研究显示走路多、开车少能降低意外死亡风险，但这可能并非因为健身的直接效果。
• riskassessment指出，随机意外死亡的风险涉及两个概率：事故发生的概率和事故中死亡的概率。他认为健身可能与这两个概率都有关联，特别是降低事故中死亡的概率。
• gregors提到，研究基于瑞典男性的数据，他们的健康水平远高于普通美国人，因此结果可能不适用于美国人群。
• amluto认为健身可能降低车祸死亡风险，原因包括运动对神经系统疾病的预防作用，如阿尔茨海默病可能增加车祸风险。
• ohelabs强调，美国人的不健康生活方式和肥胖率较高，因此研究结果对美国人可能不适用，但健身确实能显著延长寿命。
• knuckleheadsmif指出，健身能提高生活质量，即使不一定延长寿命。
• ninetyninenine认为，发现随机关联并不能证明或否定因果关系，研究结果在逻辑上没有直接结论。
• deadbabe提到，很多人优化生活方式只考虑到50岁左右，因为他们对老年生活缺乏积极预期。
• _dain_怀疑研究结果，认为不健身的人可能更多依赖开车，因此涉及更多车祸。此外，不健康的人在紧急情况下生存几率可能更低。

补充讨论：
• 研究中使用瑞典男性数据，其健康水平和生活方式可能与美国等其他国家人群有显著差异，导致结果的普适性受到质疑。
• 讨论中多次提到健身与随机意外死亡之间的潜在关联，包括反应能力、生存能力和驾驶习惯等具体论据。
• 对高强度锻炼的价值存在争议，部分人认为适度锻炼已经足够，而过度的锻炼可能带来的收益有限。
• 生活质量和健康寿命在讨论中被视为比单纯的长寿更为重要的目标，反映出人们对老年生活质量的关注。

44024843.article_content:
The effect of physical fitness on mortality is overestimated
Pressmeddelande
2025-05-15
In the study, the researchers used different methods to examine the association between fitness level in late adolescence and premature death. Photo: Getty Images
That fit people have a reduced risk of premature death from various diseases is a recurring result in many studies. New research from Uppsala University shows that people with high fitness levels in their late teens also have a reduced risk of dying from random accidents. This suggests that the associations seen in previous studies have probably been misleading.
Many observational studies have shown that people who exercise more and have good cardiorespiratory fitness early in life are at lower risk of premature death from causes such as cancer and cardiovascular disease. However, a new study published in the European Journal of Preventive Cardiology suggests that the association between physical fitness and a reduced risk of mortality may be misleading.
“We found that people with high fitness levels in late adolescence had a lower risk of dying prematurely, for example from cardiovascular disease, compared to those with low fitness levels. But when we looked at their risk of dying in random accidents, we found an almost similarly strong association. This suggests that people with high and low fitness levels may differ in other important ways, which is something that previous studies have not fully taken into account,” says Marcel Ballin, associated researcher in epidemiology and lead author of the study.
Based on conscription data from over 1 million men
In the study, the researchers leveraged data from 1.1 million Swedish men who were conscripted for military service between the years 1972 and 1995. The men, who were on average 18 years old at the time of conscription, were divided into five groups based on their fitness level at the time. They were then followed until their 60s or until they died. With access to the National Cause of Death Register, the researchers were able to see their cause of death. They subsequently used different methods to study the association between fitness level in late adolescence and premature death.
The researchers started with a traditional analysis of mortality from cardiovascular disease, cancer and from all causes, as in previous observational studies. They adjusted their statistical models for factors such as BMI, age at conscription, year of conscription, and parents’ income and education level. The results showed that the group with the highest fitness level had a 58 per cent lower risk of dying from cardiovascular disease, a 31 per cent lower risk of dying from cancer, and a 53 per cent lower risk of dying from all causes, compared with the group with the lowest fitness level.
Very similar risk of dying in random accidents
Next, the researchers examined how fitness was associated with the risk of dying in random accidents such as car accidents, drownings and homicides. They chose random accidents because they assumed that there ought to be no association between the men’s fitness in late adolescence and the risk of dying in random accidents. This method is called negative control outcome analysis and involves testing the validity of your results for a primary outcome by comparing them with an outcome where no association ought to be found. If, however, an association is found, it may indicate that the groups studied are not actually comparable, and that the study suffers from what is typically referred to as confounding. The researchers found that men with the highest fitness levels had a 53 per cent lower risk of dying in random accidents. Yet, it is unlikely that the men’s fitness would have such a big effect on their risk of dying in random accidents.
These results were also confirmed when the researchers used the sibling comparison design. Using this method, the researchers compared the risk of premature death between siblings with different fitness levels to control for all the factors that the siblings share such as behaviours, environmental factors, and some genetic factors.
“It surprised us that the association with accidental mortality reflected the other associations, even after we controlled for all the factors that siblings share. This underlines how strong the assumptions are that you make in observational studies, since it appears to be very difficult to create comparable groups. The consequences may be that you overestimate the magnitudes of the effects you find,” says Marcel Ballin.
Picture confirmed in other studies
The study is one of the largest of its kind in which researchers used negative control outcomes to investigate whether the associations between fitness and mortality are in fact valid. The results in this study are also supported by other research.
